utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the outset, let me say that in the absence of Judge David, Judge Van Den Wyngaert and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Mr. Groome, are you to -- is there a preliminary matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There were two brief ones, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One, yesterday, Madam Registrar advised me that there was a document. This is the compendium of photographs that Mr. McCoy had taken and selected that was a part of his report, 1D22-0603, which I had neglected to tender to the Chamber. I was told that there was a marked and an unmarked copy, a marked copy that I guess the witness had marked up in the course of either the direct or the cross-examination and that I need to tender one or the other. I decided to -- yeah, for purposes of preserving the full record, I think I ought to tender both the marked and the unmarked of that document as they are for all intents and purposes different documents once the markings have been added to it. The second matter, I did receive last night the video-tape that Mr. Groome was intending to show to the witness when we had taken the break, when we had taken the break yesterday. Two things with respect to that. The video I received is sound bytes. It's not a continuous video, so to the extent there is raw footage, I believe we will be entitled to that under the disclosure rules. But the portions of the video that I do have have this individual who's sitting in the courtroom today. I believe his name is Mr. Sexton, that can be corrected if I'm wrong. It has him testifying on the video making assertions and rendering opinions as to what we are seeing, et cetera. Now, this gentleman is not on the witness either as fact witness or as an expert witness or as a rebuttal witness. It is out-of-court testimony that has been presented, we believe, for the truth of the matter asserted, and it is being presented to a witness. So we have an out-of-court declarant statement being present to a witness, which I thought was something that we had previously -- that previously had been ruled to be impermissible. Now, again, and we're being presented it without cross, and we don't know this man's qualifications as to whether he is an expert. So if the video-type is to be relied upon in any way as to the spoken portion of it, we believe it would be a violation of Rules 92 bis and 94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You know my predilection. It is to take the points when the matters arise. So let us see the video and let me see the individual who --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. I just want to make that at the outset, number one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers not speak at the same time. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no preliminary matters, Your Honour -- [overlapping speakers] ... JUDE ROBINSON: {Overlapping speakers] ... let the witness be brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm prepared to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm admitting the exhibits of Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D22-0603 will become Exhibit 1D195, Your Honours, and the marked copy will become 1D196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I be told why the witness is late, the Court Deputy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The Court Deputy is investigating the late arrival of the witness, and we'll inform you as soon as we have more information, and I'd like that to go on the record when we do get the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, before I pick up where I left off yesterday, you had said that it was the policy of fire investigators to destroy their notes once they issue a report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, through the magic of the internet, we were able to actually download the Standard Operating Guidelines for the Albuquerque Fire Department. I'm going to hand it up to you, and I believe that you testified that you were in part one of the authors of this document. Could I ask you to please show us the section where it says that are you to destroy your notes after you file your report.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, before you start there, I don't know where it's at in there. I helped draft them up, and then they got turned in to my captain, submitted to administration. I have not yet seen the new ones that have come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You're more familiar with this document than I am. Perhaps you could look through the table of contents or the index, and could you show us where it says that a fire investigator should destroy his or her notes once they have drafted a report. And while you're looking through that, do you recognise that as the Standard Operating Guidelines of Albuquerque?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is, I believe, a portion of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps in order to save time, could I ask you maybe to hold on to that copy. If you would be so good as to during the next break spend some of the time looking through it, and then perhaps when you return from the break you can let us know where it is, okay?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you said you had FBI training with respect to investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Post-blast investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In that course, did the FBI teach the destruction of notes after a report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No note-taking or anything like that was covered in it. It was just identifying explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to just ask you a follow-up question about the piece of wood that was embedded in the concrete about 7 feet off the floor that we talked about yesterday. My question to you is, did it appear to you to be a piece of wood that had already been charred and jammed into the concrete, or did it appear to be a piece of wood that was in the concrete when it became charred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it was 6 feet above, and it didn't appear to be jammed in because I was able to just simply remove it. There was a gap around the edges of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it appeared to be present in the concrete when the concrete was placed before it set; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. I couldn't make that determination. Again, it wasn't set in there such as that beam under the window. That one you could tell was affixed when it was plastered. This one was just simply sitting there. There was a gap above it as it was sitting in the bottom. Then as I would just reach in, pull it out, so it not like I had to pry it out or force it out. So it was not plastered in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you actually took out the piece of charred wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you do with the piece of charred wood that you took out?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I did the other ones; I felt it, examined it, and determined it was a piece of charred wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you do with it then?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I placed it back in the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm going to ask that you -- well, you talked about that beam now. Yesterday, you said when I asked you the question: "How did you come to the conclusion that it was actually embedded in the concrete wall?" And your answer was: "Because the concrete is flush with the edges of it." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that you now take a look at clip 090321, Pionirska overview, wall C. There's a video going to be shown on the screen in front of you. After you look at it, I'm going to ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Voiceover: "This area with the two windows, large windows, is deemed area or wall C, and it also has an electrical -- it also has an electrical junction or junction box with chase running down the wall, curving over under the window. As you can see, there's vine that we haven't removed. Below the window-sill --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a minute. Please stop the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Per the Court's instructions, this is the point we were talking about, is if the declarant on the video has not been identified as the witness, has not been tendered pursuant to a motion to amend, is the testimony improper at this point and a violation of Rules 92 or 94?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not offering the testimony. I'm just seeking to impeach the witness and be entitled to impeach the witness with anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can finish my comments to His Honour. I'd be entitled to impeach with any video, whether it was by someone who works for OTP or for a video taken by any source. It's -- until the time that I intend or try to seek it as evidence in my case, I think that's when the issues of hearsay and that all come. I'm simply using it to challenge this witness and whether his conclusion that the wood was embedded in the concrete wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, and Your Honour, but as we can see, the tape is becoming part of the record. The court reporter is taking down what's on the video-tape, and the Court has already ruled it improper to impeach a witness with a statement of another witness. And I'm going to assume that Mr. Groome out of the magic of the voice of whoever is on here is going to claim that whatever's said on this video-tape is true, regardless of the training or background of the declarant or why he's being offered, and that is improper. And it is an out-of-court statement being used to impeach an in-court witness improperly. At the very least, he should have an opportunity to review the statement, review the evidence; he is an expert. And then Mr. Groome can put to him the statements. But otherwise, otherwise the record is going to be full of what is ever on this tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, may I adopt one of your favorite expressions. Mr. Groome, what is missing is the, what is it, foundational matters. Who is this? And we haven't heard anything as to what is going on and who is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the person who's speaking on the tape is an investigator by the name of Mr. Garry Selsky. He's sitting behind me in the court. He accompanied me to Visegrad this past weekend to verify some of this testimony that was introduced last week just to take a look at whether or not it was corroborated by what we saw. We can as easily play this tape silently if the Court wishes, but I submit -- you know, I always remember when I was in law school my evidence teacher saying, You know, you can impeach a witness with a slice of pizza to make the point that really an impeachment, it a -- really anything you're entitled to put to a witness to see if it challenges their conclusions or their assumptions. I'm not seeking to tender this evidence at this point. I'm simply asking the witness to look at this, and then I'm going to ask him whether it changes his conclusion that this piece of wood is embedded in the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But we haven't heard who is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will see the images without any voice. That's the Chamber's ruling. And then you can put questions to the witness on the basis of the images.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm just setting that up now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, what we're looking at at .22 seconds on this image, that's the electric box that's to the upper left-hand corner of the window in the room; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell with the blurriness. It looks similar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, you were there. What was it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the electrical box.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That was the electrical box, okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the piece of wood that we're looking at, that's the beam that you referred to that was embedded in the wall; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if we could pause the video now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, as we can see from this image, in the centre of this, there's actually an inch gap between the wall and the piece of wood; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this one, yes. If you go back to about .47 to the edge of it, you can see the plaster directly to the edge of the beam.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it your evidence now that it was partially embedded in the wall or completely embedded in the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I believe earlier I did state yesterday that the walls had been falling apart and degredated [phoen]. This was attached, but it's obvious, you can see the walls have been collapsing around this. But if you look at the edges, the edges are smooth and flush with the wall. If you want to go back to .47 or in that area --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's continue on. Please continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this is not a piece of furring strip?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. We can stop the video there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at one more video.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, if you want to go back to just about maybe four seconds, it shows the edge flush with the wall again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next video shows the edge very good, and that's PO Evid, wall C.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, what's being taken out of the the wall is the electric box; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's the same area, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you take a close look at this electric box?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just examined the hole and determined that it was some sort of junction box based on the wires going into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any opinion as to whether the material was burnt or not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I determined that it was a black hole with wires going into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And black, you mean -- black is sometimes associated with burning. Did you believe it was burnt?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We can see the bag being sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, on the video we can observe at 2. -- 2 minutes, 13 seconds, investigator Selsky writing on the board, the embedded beam.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is Mr. Groome a witness? And, if so, let's move to disqualify the OTP. Let's make him a witness. And let's go on with that. Mr. Groome should not be tendering this video, and if Mr. Groome took this video, I move to make Mr. Groome a witness, and I move to add him to my 65 ter. And I make the motion to disqualify the Prosecutor right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you are not to comment on the tape in the manner which you just did because that breeches the ruling that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, based on what we're watching now, isn't it true that this piece of wood --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That was on the transcript. I just spoke. But my words have been, but my words have been attributed to Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, it was not a beam embedded in the concrete, was it? It was a nailed to the concrete, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply stated that it was a piece of wood embedded in the wall. It is not a furring strip. A furring strip is made to hold other items up, such as wooden planks. Is it your contention that this interior of the room had wood interior wall?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's what I want to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if I could ask the usher's assistance to actually show Mr. Dimas that piece of wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, I'm going to ask you to take a look at that piece of wood. Please be careful. It has nails on it. Is that the piece of wood that you described as a beam that was pristine embedded in the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the wood that I saw that was embedded in the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the common usage of embed is it's inside the wall.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this was inside the plastered area. As the video showed, it was flush on the edges.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the top of the piece of board, the side with the writing on it, there are a number of nails that are partially on the other side, the side with the writing on the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There are a number of nails that are partially in the board; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that not consistent with other material being affixed to this piece of wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the majority of those nails are coming from the backside, so how would you nail something from the backside when it's in the wall such as this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, could we do this. Could you place it down on the side that was facing the concrete wall.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, like that. That's good. That's very helpful. Now, can you please point to the nails that are partially protruding from the board.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have several here, here, and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These here, here, are from the backside. These are nailed from the backside. These are from the backside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please point to any nail where the head of the nail is facing towards us.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two, this one, and this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that not consistent with something at some point having been affixed to the top of this board?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I have never denied that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that Your Honours take a look at this board if the usher could allow the Chamber to see the board as well as Defence counsel, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If we're injured by the nail, who is responsible?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There are plenty of lawyers in the court that may assist you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, is that not a piece of furring strip that is commonly used as substrate for attaching finished wall materials?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say what that would be used for. It's simply -- basically, what is that, three-quarter inch by, maybe, 3-inch piece of wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it a beam?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe my terminology was wrong. It's a piece of wood. It's a furring strip -- the furring strip's used where I'm from are usually just 1-by-2s.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So this would be an inch wider than the furring strip that you would be used that; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So aside from it being an inch wider, it essentially would be the same as a furring strip that you and I would be familiar with in the US; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Again, I looked at the beam with the totality of everything. You have one beam, you're talking about the furring strip for putting up a wood-type of wall. Now, are we to believe that you have one furring strip underneath one wall instead of all walls?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, sir, isn't it possible -- isn't it possible that if someone were -- if there were a finished material on this wall that was burnt and someone was attempting to conceal what happened there, they removed all of the burnt material, all of the furring strips, and overlooked this piece of furring strip underneath the window? Isn't that a possibility that you considered?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Again --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm just asking is it something you considered.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I did, and I'm explaining how I considered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we looked at the totality of it. We looked to see what fire damage there was, and again, you're talking about more wood within the structure. You're talking walls of wood that they had removed, and there is no signs or evidence of large-scale debris in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you did not consider the fact that all of the debris could have been taken away?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at that time, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you not consider that if they were trying to conceal what took place there that they would not have only taken the debris down but they would have shipped it or taken it out of the room?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the fact that the whole corner that was still left, that had the small burns that we showed yesterday, you still had partial floor. If you're going to remove it and clean the scene, why not do the entire room? You're going to leave one-third of the room still intact?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Or perhaps someone came in and used it afterwards for a different purpose. I'm finished with that. Thank you very much. Now, I'm going to ask that you take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Groome. I'm not sure I understand what a furring strip is. Could someone explain to me what a furring strip is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please explain how would you would -- how we would use a furring strip in the US. Let's say if you were going to finish a basement in the US, how would you use a furring strip?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally what you do is you attach small planks of wood around the whole wall area so you can affix your wood finish over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now and -- would I not be correct in saying that the wood is ordinarily placed horizontally, parallel with the floor and the ceiling?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then the fixed finish is put up above it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct also.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the only difference between a furring strip that you and I are familiar with and this piece of wood is that this piece of wood is one inch wider than a furring strip that we would be used to?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also shorter, and it's one piece, and it's not the whole length of the wall. Usually you put in the whole length of the wall because you're going to finish the entire wall. You're not going to finish just the area beneath your window.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there were several electric boxes in the walls, and we've seen one on the tape. You saw no burning -- evidence of burning in those electric boxes?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there were grooves cut in the wall, were there not, where the wire from those electric boxes were placed; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm sorry. Are you talking about where the wire was?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, the person on the video-tape from the electric box runs their pen down the side of the wall, and then it curves over towards the window.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That was a groove where there was wiring placed, was that not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We found that the wires were plastered directly into the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. You -- are you saying that you could not see the groove left by the wires?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I saw the grooves, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And that was burnt, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you looked at the wiring and made a determination that there was no evidence of burning on the insulation or whatever remained of that wire?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- we noted that it was melted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The wire was melted?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So when we look from the top of that electric box and we travel down the wall, you made the conclusion that the insulation in there had melted?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In parts of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could both speakers slow down, please, and make a brief pause between question and an answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you put that in your report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you not put -- let me ask you this. We can see those grooves -- now, I'm familiar with the word "chase," wire chase. Is that the word that you would use?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What word would you use for the -- where wires are placed in a concrete wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, wire chases usually refer to the conduit or piping or an opening such as -- and a lot of times older homes just drill holes through walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would you call that groove where the wiring is placed? Should we just call it a groove?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They are in several locations in that room; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how many of them did you make the determination that there was -- the wire insulation had melted?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in two different areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And so when you looked at this room, you found in two locations the wiring embedded in the concrete walls melted, and you did not put that in your report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you not put it in your report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I went to the totality of everything and the amount of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask that you -- with the usher's assistance that you take a look at a bag. It's an evidence bag, and if it could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we would object to this form of tendering the materials to the witness. One, the witness has been already accepted by the Court as an expert in fire investigation. I looked at the bag and Mr. Groome refused to open the bags for me. The reason being is -- and the objection is that if you're going to put questions of this nature to this witness as an expert, he should be allowed to inspect the contents. The fact of the fatter is that the bags from whatever dirt, they're almost opaque at this point in time, so it makes it very suggestive without a real opportunity to examine the contents of the bag. I would object to a simple ELMO presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I fully agree with Mr. Alarid, so I'm going to ask the witness to open the bag, pour the contents on a tray, and examine it here before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going ask you -- if the usher could please place this tray on the bag. I'm going to ask that -- if it can be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] May we inspect the bag before it's emptied?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, if you wish. Let Defence counsel see the bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If the usher would show Defence counsel. The contents of some of these bags are quite fragile, so I just ask for some care to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, when the bag makes its way to you, I'm going to ask that you -- you examine the bag. You work with evidence bags all the time, do you not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you'll be able to tell whether the seal on this bag has been violated?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And -- so could I ask you to take a look at the bag, check whether or not it has been violated.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not appear to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you take a scissor, and I'm sure you're familiar with opening evidence bags, but I'm going to ask you to cut it at the bottom, not near seal, so we always have a record of the seal, and I'm going to ask you to pour the contents onto the white tray.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, what's the provenance of this bag and its contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Your Honours will recall from the video, this was the bag that was -- and we can see the same writing on the bag. Again, I'm not tendering it at this time, but it's obvious from the video that this was the material taken out of the electric box and placed in the bag. I can call up that portion of the video if Your Honour wants to compare the writing on this bag with the writing on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, that's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, can you please open the bag and just put the contents on the tray.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness opens bag]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if the bag can be returned to Investigator Selsky, he'll take care of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, can I ask you just to take a look at that, maybe flip it over to the portion that was -- now, the portion that you have in your hand now that's facing you, if you could turn it over to the other part there. Is it your evidence that there's no evidence of burning on that, no smoke damage, no evidence of burning?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that that be shown to Defence counsel and to Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, while that's being shown around, you'll remember yesterday I brought to your attention a black horizontal strip that was -- if we were inside the room looking at the door, it was on the upper left-hand portion of the wall. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you restate that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The part of the wall that I want to refer you to is, if you're standing in the centre of the room looking towards the door, the upper left-hand -- to the left of the door, the upper portion of the wall, there was a black line that ran horizontally, and you circled it yesterday. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that that be returned to Investigator Selsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Actually, we'll probably have questions, so -- I apologise. We'll probably have questions utilising it, so if we could set them out on a table so they're easily accessible, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is there a way to identify that? I ask that when we call up -- since you're not tendering it, is there some kind of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's bag C-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: C-1. Thank you, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You know the piece that I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask that you look at a piece of video-tape. It's 090321, PO Evid, wall A, number 1. And I believe you testified yesterday that you did not take a close examination of this black material in the wall. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While the video is being played, could I ask the usher, please, to place another tray next to the witness. Perhaps we can expedite the time that it's taking. And this would be the bag that's marked A-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that whatever this black material, is it's clearly embedded in the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that appears so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, as Investigator Selsky holds it up to the camera, I'd ask you just to take a look as well with the bag next to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at the bag next to you. Does it appear to be the same bag that we're looking at in the video?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bag appears to be the same. Could you rewind that? I didn't see where he -- it looked like he placed the bag and then he turned around and then the bag was on the other side of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you to examine the seal on that bag and see whether it appears tampered with or violated.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not, but that's not what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The witness wants a slight rewind of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could go back to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what portion do you want?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just back maybe five seconds, seven seconds. I'm sorry, maybe further. Right before -- right when we sets it down from that point on. No, prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Is that rewound enough?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Play it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appears he -- I'm sorry. To me, it appears he places it on his left, he turns, and then it's in a different position, but -- this is the bag that you did bring up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Is the seal violated?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does counsel wish to see it before I ask Mr. Dimas to cut it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to cut the bag open and empty the contents on the ...

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness empties bag]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And again, if the bag could be given to Mr. Selsky. Could I ask you to examine the contents of this bag and tell us whether or not there's charred material in that bag.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears there are a few chunks in there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Of charred wood? Are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that it be shown to the Chamber and to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, so far now we have the charred wood that you found up in the wall, 6 feet above, we have the melted insulation in two places in the wall, and now we have charred wood from an area -- how high would this be off the floor?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It'd probably be up to the same as the other one, about 6 feet up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So about 6 feet off the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. If that could be returned to Mr. Selsky. Now I want to move to the floor. Could I ask that the following video be played for Mr. Dimas: 090321, PO Evid, floor. And I'm going to ask that the tray with bag F-1 be given to Mr. Dimas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see the video, Mr. Dimas?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise where in the room we are in this video?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, could I ask you -- could we put another tray with bag with F-2 right on the table in front of you. Both of them have to do with the floor. I think maybe we can expedite matters by having you deal with both of them at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, can you explain to us, how would it be that a piece of wood embedded in the wall would become charred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Are you talking that it's already there, somebody placed it there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's assume for the moment that the wood wasn't -- no one built a structure with charred wood but that they built it with whole wood and it became charred after. What are the different ways that a wood embedded in the concrete wall could become charred?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would just ask for a clarification. Are we talking about the one 6 feet off the ground, or are we talking about one in the apparent closed-in doorway or window as it appears?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm just asking you theoretically for the moment. What are the different ways, if you were investigating a scene and you found a piece of wood that was obviously fully embedded in concrete and you found it charred, what are the different possible ways theoretically that it -- could it become charred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be charred due to heat transfer. It could be done by a direct flame. If there's any electrical wiring nearby, conductivity through the electrical wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it sounds like the three ways you've described -- heat transfer, so you mean heat in the room of sufficient heat -- of sufficient temperature to char that wood; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sounds about right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what temperature would the heat in the room have to be to char the piece of wood in the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the extent of the char.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Similar to what you saw in the last exhibit, that charring.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You really can't say. Depends on the wood, how dry it is, the humidity factor, moisture content, type of wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would be the lowest possible temperature at which that wood would char?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd probably say maybe a thousand degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: A thousand degrees. What would happen to the human if the human was in the room at the same time that whatever heat was in the room that charred that wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They'd be burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you also said it could happen by direct contact with flame; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if the flames themselves were actually touching the wood, that would cause charring?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then the final way that you said was that if there was some kind of electrical problem with electrical wires running, what, adjacent to the wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adjacent, or if like in the States a nail might have punctured the wire and it would be conducted through that nail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that would cause in the wood.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now can I ask you -- let's do F-1 first. That's the one on the ELMO to your left. Could I first ask you again, check the seal of the bag.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to open it as you have before and place it on the tray.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness empties bag]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to repeat the same exercise for F-2 before you. Please check the seal on the bag in front of you. When you're satisfied it hasn't been violated, open it up and place the contents on the tray.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while Mr. Dimas is doing that, I'm reminded to ask the Chamber when we might expect the source material for Dr. Hough since he's going to be called imminently. We would like an opportunity to review that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had already tendered all source materials for Dr. Hough. He did not ever review the recordings that Mr. Ivetic made, nor has he ever had an opportunity to review them. And so from that standpoint we consider the ruling as is, and we had already given the Prosecution all the statements and materials that we believe he had had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe there were 194 quotes contained in the report. Was there not some kind of notes with which he was able to -- that he made during the interview where he recorded these statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sure he has personal notes, but that's his personal notes. That's not source material. And that's not stuff we gave him. Source material implies that we gave it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, then I would ask the Chamber for a clarification as to whether the material envisaged by the Chamber to be turned over included notes taken by Dr. Hough during the interviews of Mr. Lukic upon which he made his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll tender that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, let's start with the tray that's F-1. Would you agree with me that is not burnt? That's the one right in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And F-2, could you look at that, and what is your opinion as to whether that piece of wood shows evidence of charring?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one has more of the appearance of just heavy moisture and rotting away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it possible that it could be charred and that in the 17 years subsequently that moisture has also caused it to rot?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With char, you'd still be able to notice the char, even in moist wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So it's your evidence that there's no evidence of charring on this?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that the two trays be held up for the Chamber and for Defence counsel to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, then I -- just a couple of more things I'd like you to take a look at. I want to now move to the area where you said you saw some charred material in the wall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, where did that come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the video -- hopefully it was clear to Your Honours. If you were watching the video, it was picked up from the floor, of the area where there was dark wood in the -- I can replay the video if you wish. Both these pieces, one was collected from the area of the floor where there did not appear to be any dark wood, the other where there was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I make a comment, Your Honour? I never --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never disputed that we found fire and charred wood on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'm not challenging you, but so is your evidence that you did find charred wood on the floor but that this wood here is not the wood that you found that was charred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if they could be returned to Investigator Selsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going show you two clips, and this relates to the area where you said -- you've already said you found charred wood, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could video-clip 09321, evidence character, wall E, number 1 be played. Your Honour, can everyone see this video?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to see the video, sir? No? Let's try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't know if all the switches are in place where they need to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the still image on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before we play it, is this the area where you found the charred wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there are two indentations in the wall there. Which one is the place where you found the charred wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one on the left there where the finger's pointing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Let's watch the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll ask the usher before you sit down, unless you have a task to attend to, I'd ask that you place another tray in front of Mr. Dimas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that we place bag E-1 on the ELMO in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we pause for a second. Your Honour, I'm going to ask that we put the sound on now. Although there's no commentary by the investigator, there are some sounds of wood breaking that I think will help the Chamber come to a view as to whether this wood was simply loose in there or actually had to be broken out of where it was embedded in the wall. So with the Court's permission, I would ask that we play that -- play the sound, and of course, if anything is said, I would ask that it be disregarded. But I think the sound of the wood being taken out of the wall would be relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While that's being done, Mr. Dimas, we can see a screwdriver being used to probe the depth of that hole. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that the second clip, number 2, be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And sir, could I ask you again to maybe have sight of the bag when the video is playing just so I can ask you if you're able to see that it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, as you see it come out of the wall, do you have any view from what you see in the video whether or not this appears to be charred wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe I stated there was charred wood up in that corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But I believe your testimony is that it was loose; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the hole on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you notice this hole on the right-hand side? Did you explore this hole when you were there?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was all actually encompassed in one area. It appeared to be adjoining hole. I didn't have any tools present so I took the easiest route and looked at a piece I was able to pull out and examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you ordinarily go to a fire scene to do an evaluation without any tools?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, if we could pause right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, the video indicates someone withdrawing a screwdriver, holding it up to a measuring tape, and it being approximately 6 inches. Would you agree that that's the approximate depth of that hole?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, assumes facts not in evidence, and the Prosecutor's testifying. And I don't believe that the video showed anywhere near that, and so we would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you'd have to ask him whether he agrees --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe that's what I did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able from your observations - you've already told us you had no tools - but does it seem reasonable to you that this piece of wood embedded in the wall could have gone back as far as approximately 6 inches?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, we would have to replay it. I wasn't concentrating --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- could we play back a little bit of this. Just watch the screwdriver when it's fully inserted. Maybe back a little bit further. Okay, that's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you want us to pause anywhere? Let us know.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine right there. As you can see, it's being taken at an angle, so he's able to fit the whole screwdriver in there, and I already stated that the two holes appeared to connect to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So what would be your approximation of how deep into the concrete this depression in it -- into the wood was?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about how deep. It's not the 6 inches you're describing because it's at an angle. He's going elongated instead of straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to just watch the video now for the sealing of the bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you to examine the bag next to you.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the front of the bag. I'm sorry. It just showed a signature on the back or initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, perhaps flip the bag over and see ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. We could pause there. Back up just a few frames.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to examine the bag and tell us whether you recognise that -- what's visible on the screen is the back of the bag.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Can I ask you to check the seal on the bag.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The seal's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now can I ask you to open it and place the contents on the table.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness empties bag]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I ask you to examine the contents of the bag and give us your opinion as to whether or not that's charred wood.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a combination of charred and moisture, same as -- yes. Same as the one next to it, which I've already accepted. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you seem to have reached that conclusion in about five seconds. Is it that obvious that it's charred wood or ...

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Could I ask that that be shown to the Chamber and to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, you agree with me, it's not an insignificant amount of charred wood, is it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In itself, it is. For an entire room, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, now we have it on two locations in the room. It's 6 feet -- at least 6 feet off the floor, so it can't be the result of any small fire for boiling a kettle or cooking some food, can it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- well, it depends. If one of the fires took off, burned up some more of the room, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But if one of the fires took off and burned up some more of the room, then we have a fully-involved fire in the room, do we not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but again, we don't know when that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So you now agree that it is possible that there was a fully involved fire in that room?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly at some point, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We don't know. We'd have to look at other evidence to determine when that fire occurred, but we can now clearly say that the evidence that we find in this room is consistent with a fire being fully involved in that room.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you restate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What you're saying now seems somewhat different than your report. It seems now you're allowing for the possibility that this evidence is consistent with a fire in that room that was sufficiently involving the entire room to cause charring in two places 6 feet above the ground.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible, but, again, you could have fire in different location. We've reviewed, and your own statements, about the fire on the exterior because we don't know when that happened, 'cause the existing shed. Your video also showed that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's focus the physical evidence --

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me finish.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers, please not overlap. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By your video that was taken in 2001, it showed that that structure was being utilized by someone. For what purpose, we don't know. We don't know when the fire took place. They're occupying it at that time in 2001. Now you stated the fire that was inside the shed, and I'm not talking about the shed under the portico, I'm talking the structure itself was being utilised in 2001 by your own video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But sir, your expertise wasn't brought to this courtroom to say when a fire occurred. Your expertise was called upon to say whether or not there was a fire inside the room; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was brought to determine if there was a fire involved in the room and if it could be stated -- by the statements. If it was consistent --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you to just confine yourself -- let's put the statements aside for a moment and confine yourself to the physical evidence from the room, okay? Given that we've now found charred wood by your admission on two walls in the room, how far apart are these two areas where the charred wood was recovered?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 10 -- 10 feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long is the overall length of the room?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eighteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it seems to cover most of the room, no?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if those two pieces of wood embedded at 6 feet in the wall became charred at the same time, would that the not lead us to the conclusion that the room was involved in a fire of at least a thousand degrees to cause the charring?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about a fire of that considerable amount --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I would object to the classification that they were charred at the same time. I don't think there's any way that the Prosecution has established that, and I believe that's speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm allowed to ask an expert such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But then he's asked and answered the question as to possibility and probability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Listen, you both, you fire from two cylinders at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue, sir.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you restate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question was: "And if those pieces of wood embedded at six feet in the wall charred at the same time, would that not lead us to a conclusion that the room was involved in a fire of at least a thousand degrees to cause that charring?"

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, if you're talking about a fire of that magnitude, it would encompass the entire room. We would not have clean wood still left in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Aside from that -- so what would be the other reasonable possibilities for wood embedded in concrete, there from the time the structure was built, presumably, to become charred? What would be the other reasonable possibilities?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I don't understand. Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, you've told us the three ways they can become charred is an electrical fault, a direct flame, or a heat transfer from the room; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So can you give us a theoretical scenario where the room is not engulfed in flames and these two wood at both location becomes charred?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were separate fires during the course of when the structure was built, or not built but being occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you believe it's possible in a room 18 feet wide -- how -- I'm sorry, long. How wide was it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thirteen feet wide, that there could be a fire that would raise the temperature in one part of the room to 1.000 degrees but not impact the other wood 10 feet away. Is that what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you think it's possible that someone put out that fire and then at some other point in time, there was another fire in the room in front of that piece that raised the temperature to 1.000 degrees and did not impact the rest of the room?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a case like that?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, is it still your evidence that what we see before us on the tray was not significant enough to put in your report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm going to ask that -- if the usher could return that to Mr. Selsky. I'm going to ask that you look at a video of the outside of the window frame. Now, you've said on your -- page 2 of your report under 1(A), you state: "Exterior showed no signs of fire venting upward as would occur in a structure fire." Correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at a video. This is from -- well, it's 090321, PO outside of window. And I'm going to ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to pause it at 16 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise where we are?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's the first window.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, we see some black and grey at the upper corner of that window under the vines that are growing there. Sir, is that not consistent with the type of smoke damage that we would find in a violent fire?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice it to be smoke damage when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you notice it at all?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed some discolouration due to the water content.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that that's water on the concrete?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Water, moisture, mold.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you get up to --

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm still talking. Mold, the contents of the dirt flowing down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you got up to examine it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't climb up there. I observed it from the ground level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you made those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we go on to 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's still your evidence that that could not be smoke damage?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not appear to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How would smoke damage look different from what we're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- I don't know how to describe it. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it a different colour? Is it a different shape?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varies in colours. What you're seeing here is some grey with a couple of black spots.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would smoke damage look like to us?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually similar colours. Again, have you to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So the colours are similar to smoke damage?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is different about how smoke damage would appear that made you conclude that this was not smoke damage?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just looking at the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You're talking about the inside again?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, inside, exterior, just like underneath the portico or whatever it's called, that area, we assumed that that was heavy smoke damage, when, in fact, we found a lot of mold under there. Just because it's so dark, we -- at first, initially, we thought it was smoke damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going ask that you be -- a picture could be placed on the ELMO. This is a still of the video taken or tendered by Mr. Ivetic yesterday as 1D184. Now, I'm going to ask you to look at the same top left corner and ask you to circle it. See the top upper left corner of the window?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle that, please. Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, do you agree with me that there seems to be some darkening in the same area up at the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And in 2001, it seems the structure was in better shape, and there's no obvious signs of wetness on this structure, is there?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not appear. This is actually a good photo because what you see in normal venting would be an entire pattern coming off in the -- in the full length here. All you're seeing is one little corner. If it's fully involved, it's going be venting out this window, off each end.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would happen, let's say the person --

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm still --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue, sir.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you look out this -- this window here, we'd see a V-pattern coming out of it. We'd see this whole area here. As we know, smoke would be billowing out, if it was fully involved. So all we see is a dark discolouration here. If it's a fully involved fire, or as we've been discussing, reaching a thousand degrees, we'd see black smoke. Anyone who's seen a fire sees black smoke coming out. Witnesses -- one of the witnesses stated she --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, now you're starting to talk about -- I've asked you -- sorry. I've asked you a specific question about the window. I have another question for you.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If only part of the window was broken, that the person who broke this window, maybe it was two panes, we don't know, but if only a portion of the window was broken, is it not fair to say that only smoke would billow out of the portion of the window that was broken?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would not be the case. Once it become fully involved, the entire window would have busted out and vented upward. Even if it was only one smaller pane, by the statement, that window was broken out by one of the witness that she escaped through. Even if we just state for one second that was top corner that she escaped from, how small was the window that she escaped from to vent this fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence -- do you have any professional opinion as to what is the darkening in the upper left-hand corner of this window?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. I was not there in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Before we finish with this picture, can we zoom out just a little bit. Sir, we see, do we not, that it appears that some plastic sheeting has been used to cover the window?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do we also not see that it appears to be the end of a bed frame?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a bed frame and some wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm finished with that. Could we call up on e-court Y020-3507.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, is there a way to identify that document so I can use it in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I would tender that, Your Honour. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm going to take the break at 20 minutes to 11.00 at which time you will have about 20 minutes left for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I should finish within that time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and we will break at about 12.00 or 10 past 12.00. As I indicated yesterday, all judges have a plenary to attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that Judge David is not here this morning, could I ask it be communicated to him that Mr. Selsky will remain here in the courtroom with the evidence on the table should he wish to see it after which time Mr. Selsky is going to preserve the chain of custody, put it in new evidence bags, but of course we could always open bags at a later time if Judge David wanted to look at it, but I'll have Mr. Selsky remain here during the break with the evidence on the trays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, now, it seems that everyone is in agreement that there was a fully involved fire on the upper floors on this house; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, in this picture we see the rear of the house, do we not?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- what do you mean the rear?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, we're looking from where the gully is up towards the house.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be basically the north-east -- no, north-west corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And we're looking at below are the two windows of the basement room that we were just discussing.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw your attention to the lentils of the first-floor window. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you considering the lentils?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: See the concrete structures at the -- see the openings where the bricks have fallen out?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you go to the top row of bricks.
