utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you see the two concrete structures in between?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle them so that it's clear to everyone in the courtroom what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, are these not lentils that are used to support windows in a building?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please indicate -- well, let me ask you, do you see any smoke plume damage from the fires that we all agree occurred on the first and second floor above the lentils of the first-floor windows?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, do not. There could be many explanations for this. I'm not sure if this building was completed as far as construction, if there was a roof on it, if the back area was open. There could be many reasons why it wasn't venting that direction. If it has another path, that's the way it'll go, whereas in the basement there was no other way for the smoke and heat to escape other than the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. But you do agree there's no smoke damage above the windows on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it not possible that after 17 years of snow, rain, wind, sun, the elements that the weather has eradicated the smoke?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say no in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence, then, that smoke would not -- for whatever reason that you're not sure of, smoke did not come out of the rear windows of this house?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. On that first ground floor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to now ask you to look at a video, 090321, PO overview, door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, now, let's not talk about the wood for a moment. Let's talk about the blackened area of the concrete above the door. Is that not smoke damage to the door?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found it to be mostly mold and blackening from the mold.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this the surface you described as wet and mouldy?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does it appear as it appeared to you that day?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that looks wet to you?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to tell from the video. It's much easier to be on-site, physically touch it, examine it. Just as I stated from the initial photographs, I had other ideas until I actually got on-scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that's -- you're absolutely certain was not smoke damage?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How would smoke damage look? How would it be different from what we see here?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you'd see different patterns. You'd see the area underneath it where it would be coming out. All you have -- it's black -- it's hard to -- it's just black on the edge of your line there above the wood frame. If it's billowing out, it'd be rolling underneath it. So all you have is some greyish areas in that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, this is a surface up under an enclosed area. That can't be smoke?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you went up higher, part of it seemed to be similar to smoke, which we attributed mainly to that burnt-out corner in the portico.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This part is directly above the door; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if there was a fire in the room, smoke would contact -- we would expect smoke to contact this area as well?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we'd be seeing patterns coming out from the door rolling up -- up into that area. You don't see that. All you see is a black baseline along the edge. Again, as I stated yesterday, we look at burn patterns to show not only intensity but movement. There's nothing to show the fire moving up out the door up into there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, it's a concrete structure. It's not flammable, is it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, so that would actually be easier because the smoke would be rolling over it without actually impinging any wood and burning into the wood. The smoke would just simply roll over, so we would see more smoke and heat damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, as we watch the door here, I think you said yesterday that you really are not able to conclude whether or not this was the door back in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this might be a good time to break, but if I could just bring to Your Honours' attention perhaps for your consideration over the break, I have a message from Ms. Sartorio who will be examining Dr. Hough. I have still not had an opportunity to read carefully your decision of yesterday afternoon, but she advises me that in paragraph 24, you specifically refer to notes taken by Dr. Hough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of me now, and I confirm that it says the Trial Chamber will therefore proprio motu order the Defence to provide to the Prosecution any source material relied upon by Dr. Hough in writing his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Your Honour, in addition to the notes, I recall from reading the report that there was test data. There were several psychological tests. The Prosecution believes that the test data would also be covered by the Chamber's order of yesterday. I would ask for not only the notes by the test results to be provided -- the test data to be provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If the Defence has those, they are to provide it. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, you've had an opportunity now to look through the Standard Operating Guidelines. Were you able to find any section that says -- instructs fire investigators to destroy their notes?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I was not. I'm not sure if this is a complete set or not. Again, I assisted in drafting them. I didn't have any part in approving them. In our original draft, it also went into how to conduct an investigation, and that's not included in this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, do you know a person by the name of Captain Michael Diaz?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would he be your superior?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In a conversation we had with him yesterday evening asking him what would be the applicable regulations to fire investigation, he said that volume 4 there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. The Prosecutor is testifying, assumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm putting a proposition to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He's testifying about a conversation he had with a Michael Diaz, and that has not been presented. That means the Prosecutor is making himself a witness and testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, he's asking whether that person is his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, and he answered in the affirmative. Then he talks about a conversation he had with Mr. Diaz. That is an improper conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not going to allow any conversation between you and the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't spoken to Captain Diaz --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll wait and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it a fact that volume 4 that have you before you is the complete set of guidelines apply to fire investigators?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's the current listing. Again, I'm not sure what they numbered it. It's just recently come out and been made available to the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, you've now had about 25 minutes with that book in the area. Were you able to find any section that says fire investigators should destroy their notes after they file a report?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I answered no, and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, can copper wire melt in a fire?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually -- it's called beading. It's similar to melting, yes. It kind of rolls up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What temperature would the fire have to get for copper wiring to melt?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the temperature of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The burnt insulation that you described before, the copper wire was gone from that; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't inspect the wire itself. I noted the melting of what was considered the insulation, and in the one box, just that wires were protruding into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that you noted the insulation was melting. You noted that in your notes that you destroyed?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I state noting, I don't always mean I write it down. I mentally note it as well. It's something that I keep just for part of my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask that you look at -- but you noted -- okay. I'm going ask you to take a look at one more video. Then I'll ask you a couple of questions after it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could tell us what we're looking at based on your visit to the scene.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The floor of the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now what are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ceiling and the rebar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now that we've moved on to the floor section -- I mean, on to the ceiling section, did the portion of the video that showed the floor, did it fairly and accurately depict the condition of the floor as you recall it from the 29th of January?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the portion of the ceiling that we're looking at now, does this fairly and accurately represent the ceiling as you recall it from your visit on the 29th of January?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's similar. I can't say if any more fell off or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While we're watching this, can you please tell us -- you described what spalling was yesterday. What temperature would have to be reached inside a structure like this for spalling to occur?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The temperature would vary, it depends again, back on the moisture content of the concrete, how long it's been curing. There's too many factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Maybe if you would be able to give us a range. What would be the lowest temperature that spalling would be possible?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the lowest would be in freezing temperatures, so that's how much it fluctuates. You can have spalling in freezing as well as heating, so you can have spalling at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does this look like spalling that occurred from freezing?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it appears like it's been degredated, I don't know, due to moisture or why. That's why yesterday I stated that I did not include it as spalling because I can make a determination to eliminate it or include it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So let's set aside spalling from freezing for the moment. What would be the lowest temperature on the high end where it's caused by heat that would cause spalling?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, there's no upper limit. Again, it goes back to the factors of the moisture, the curing time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying the lowest. What would be the lowest temperature where we could expect spalling?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the lowest is when freezing turns to heat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm saying let's put aside freezing.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the range. It's from freezing temperatures to the maximum heat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's say the spalling was caused during a fire. What temperature would have to be occurring in the room for spalling to occur because of the fire?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be from the lowest possible heat source. Again, the temperature varies from freezing up to the highest temperature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can have spalling a small fire is what I'm trying to state, because it fluctuates so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So even a small fire could cause spalling, a fire that would be at the lower end of severity?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. McCoy said that some of what we see in the ceiling was similar to spalling. Based on your observations, does some if it appear as possibly spalling to you?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yeah. Again, I looked at it, and I couldn't rule one way or the other. That's why I did not call it spalling.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The portion of the video that we looked at on the ceiling, does that fairly and accurately reflect what you remember observing on the day that you were -- viewed the ceiling?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's very similar. The chunks missing, the rebar. You can actually see the moisture and mold on there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender just a video portion of that video-clip, not the audio portion, simply the video portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I have just two pieces of evidence I'd like to you look at. Again, with the assistance of the usher, if you could take a look at some concrete. Again, I'd ask you to examine the bag to see where -- to see if the seal has been violated.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Could I ask you to open it, and I want you to examine what's inside it.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness empties bag]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I know you have no personal knowledge of where this material came from, but could I ask you to read what's on the bag, just so the record knows -- or record is recorded to the label that the material came out of?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states that it's the portico over the entrance of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you to look at what are chips of concrete; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I draw your attention to the blackened areas on them, and my question to you is, sir, this is not mold, is it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's just grey concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sit not concrete with smoke on it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How are you so sure that it's not smoke?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you examine -- you even have black flakes of the mortar within. It's just black concrete. Concrete varies in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look on this -- on that side closely, you have darker grey there. That's darker there. It's just a different colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. But there's no mold on that, is there?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on that -- I'm sorry, Your Honours. Not on that piece, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the concrete over the door, directly over the door, it's your evidence that there was mold on that portion of the door?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was in several areas. The video shows one area that did not have mold.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If that could be returned to Investigator Selsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if I could ask you to look at one more. Again, if you could read what's on the label here.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Portico."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to check the evidence seal.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one attached to the bag or the one on the bag?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The one on the bag itself.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be sealed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to open this bag and remove its contents.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness empties bag]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, again, I know you have no personal knowledge of where this material came from, but can I ask you to assume for the purposes of my questions to you that this is the material from underneath the portico, okay. And could I ask you to look at it, turn it over, examine it. And I ask you, does it appear consistent with the material that you recall seeing under the portico?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The question that I have for you is, you see the piece that you have in your hand now? Can we focus on that piece for a minute. Can you turn that over. Can you explain to us as an expert, what is the phenomena where the side which appears to have faced the fire seems heavily charred, yet the piece behind it -- I mean, it's dirty, but it doesn't seem charred. What would be -- what would cause -- what conditions would cause that?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's considered a protected area. This one almost appears that it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to hold it a little bit more under the camera so we can see what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be one or two things. It could be a protected area. However, it looks like it was actually a thicker piece and this peeled off. Some woods are manufactured in layers, so this actually could just be peel off of another piece and that's why it didn't penetrate all the way through, just similar if we break this open, the centre would be clean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So if this is the piece under the portico, it seems that, although we seem substantial damage on the place face the fire, it seems that that finishing material actually offered some protection to the wall behind it; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure this came off the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just assume for the my -- I know you have not personal knowledge of that. Assume for the purposes of my question.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was attached to a wall, it would have offered some protection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's possible that if someone were to clean off that type of material off the wall, that the wall underneath it may not have all the indicia of a severe fire?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the term you just used.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That if there was a finished wall covering, that it could sustain heavy charring from a serious fire, but that material would offer some protection to the wall behind it. We've agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be some protection. It would go to how closely they're attached because there's no way you're going to get a finish, smooth all the way to protect the entire wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [B/C/S on the English channel] I just note that the translation seem to be coming across -- the B/C/S seems to be coming across on channel 4. But this material, since it has not burned all the way through, can offer protection to the wall behind it; correct?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm finished with that. I'd ask that that be shown to the Chamber and to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I just have really one more question for you, Mr. Dimas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I ask that both sides be shown to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, once that is returned to Investigator Selsky, I'm going to ask that a blank screen, as it were, a blank electronic piece of paper be called up for you to draw on. I'm going to ask you to draw something for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's there now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They tell me that it's in front of you now. Can we have a blank piece of paper. Could I ask you not to make any marks until I've fully explained what I'm asking you to mark, okay? Can I ask you to draw a rectangle to represent the rough dimensions of the room.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you want the windows included, door, all that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, if you could. I was going to ask you to do that next, so whichever way is easiest for you. If you could put a W for window and D for door. Okay? Now please do that.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to make it as big -- use up the entire screen, okay.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe the windows are 3 foot, 6 inches approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you measure them or ...

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just five minutes left, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's all it'll take, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've drawn a rough diagram of the wall or the room. You've put 18 feet. You've put the measurements for the windows. You're putting the width now. Okay. If I could ask you to hold off there. Now, if I could ask that we change the pen to red. That's all been done in blue. Now, I'm going to ask you to draw an X at the approximate location of where you found the charred wood on the day you examined the site, in the pocket in the wall.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that the charred wood on the floor?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So please put F, and we'll know that the circle with the F in it or the F below it is where you found charred wood on the floor. Can I ask you now on the wall, can I ask you to put an X at the approximate length of the wall where you found charred wood 6 feet above the floor.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why don't we put a 1 inside the circle so we know clearly.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, so you've put a circle with a 1 in it. Can I ask you to put a circle with a 2 in it to the location where there was black material that you did not investigate but upon examining here you recognise that it's charred material.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the one by the door?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: To the left of the door. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you put 2 next to that.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that you saw two locations where you found lines of wire where the insulation material was melted. Can I ask you to put a circle and the number 3 to indicate the approximate location of where you found that on the wall.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can I ask you to please indicate with a circle and 4 to indicate the other location where you found melted insulation in the groove containing the wiring.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I'm sorry. I don't remember where I saw that one at offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember which wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was this east wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before you -- okay.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait. I'm sorry. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Was it on one of the walls that we've already marked, or was it on one of the other? Okay. Can I ask you then to simply write in red in the middle number 4, unknown location, other wire.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, and maybe just put your initials somewhere on that diagram.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would tender that now. And it could be left up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dimas, in this relatively small room, you've now marked three locations where there's charred wood, charred insulation -- I mean melted insulation, and another site, perhaps on the same wall, perhaps on a different wall, that there was melted insulation. Is it still your evidence that there was not a fully involved fire in this room?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not consistent with the overall scene exam, the witness statements, and how their statements stated it happened, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid. Sorry, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I will try to go chronologically through the items as discussed with Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just give us an indication as to a length of your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe we're going to 12.10. Is that correct? I'm going to try and finish within that time-period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, first of all, you were asked I believe yesterday, as to concerns to the safety of the site in relation to the video-tape that was shown from 2001 when the armed individuals were escorting the investigators. Now, at that time it was postulated that the room was not examined due to potential presence of a mine or threats in the area. In the course of your work on a daily basis, do you run into the same risk when investigating sites?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. We always have to take into consideration foreseen security, especially in the case if it is an intentionally set fire or an arson fire because the person involved may still be in sight and they do not wish us to examine or make a determination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in those instances, sir, does that threat prevent you from performing your investigative duties, or do you find a way to proceed with that investigation?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, have you ever encountered unexploded incendiary devices in your line of work in your experience?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a case where one was, but any type of a situation when an explosive may be involved, we automatically call out our bomb squad and make sure everything is safe prior to entering.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And once the bomb squad arrives and diffuses the device, does the investigation proceed at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the course of your professional career, have you ever heard of an instance where investigators first arriving at a seen in 2001 would wait until 2009 to actually enter the alleged arson site to perform their investigation? Is that within the standard of protocol and procedure of an arson investigation?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. You'd want to document as much as you can as soon as you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can -- yes. If we can go to the photograph Y020-3622. I think it's much quicker to just have the photograph instead of the video that was used by the Office of the Prosecutor. And sir, is this a photograph that was taken by your investigation team with respect to the charred wood that you did find in the wall pulled out and returned in its place?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to the wood that you were able to pull out of the wall and insert back into place, did it appear to be a structural element of the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not. It just seemed like a piece of wood that may have been plastered into it by accident for some unknown reason, but I found no functionality for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about the -- what about the piece of wood to the right, the second pole? Did that appear to be a structural element of the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what is this white area between these two holes?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me? Could --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What -- what is the area -- the two holes, the dark holes, what is the lighter-coloured area between these two holes? What material is it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, it's the plaster, the concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was that plaster level with the rest of the wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, is it probable that these holes were covered by concrete and/or plaster at some time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection as to leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What conclusions do you draw based upon the empirical evidence at the scene as to whether in fact -- what the status of these holes was at some point in time earlier, for instance, in 1992 or when the building was constructed?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From looking at the walls, it had the appearance that these walls had been plastered as a finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can -- and have you ever -- strike that. I believe you were a code inspector for the fire marshal's office during -- at some point in time during your career; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of construction workers pouring concrete as their standard -- as to pouring concrete walls in specific -- in steps, not all at once?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, it's not a matter that I -- was raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, it was. Mr. Groome was bringing up alternative possibilities as to how wood could be embedded in a wall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I said I'll allow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll wait for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in the course of your experience, have you heard of construction workers, pouring concrete in a standard, that is to say with respect to walls and steps in phases, not all at once.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times concrete is poured that way. The best example would be not so much as in a building or a structure, but when they build dams. Dams are done in steps because each section has to cure, and they develop heat when the concrete is curing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is there a problem presented when temperature changes occur, what effect does the drop in temperature have on concrete that is curing?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you can develop the spalling. Again, it depends on how much water molecules are based in the concrete and at what step it's cured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And have you ever experienced in -- or heard of construction crews that are pouring concrete using methods to heat concrete while it's curing so as to prevent -- to keep it warm, to keep it from freezing and to prevent the concrete from degrading or curing improperly?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's common practice whenever you pour a concrete slab as a wall, that you use portable heaters to help cure it and set faster, especially in cold temperatures or wintertime.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me give you a hypothetical. Suppose you're in an area where there is not accessible electricity; there are no portable heaters. Are there more primitive means for heating the slabs while the concrete is curing such as --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no evidence that this expert in fire is also an expert in the placing of and curing of wet concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You asked similar questions, Mr. Groome. I'll allow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as I was saying, sir, if I could give you a hypothetical, suppose you're in an area where there's not accessible electricity, there are no portable heaters, and more primitive means have to be used, such as, perhaps, in Visegrad whenever this building was constructed. Would it be also an acceptable means to utilise open flame or wood on a slab to keep it warm while it's curing?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would, as long as it keeps the concrete warm. That helps in the curing and setting process.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Given the empirical evidence that you saw at the scene, can you exclude the possibility that this wood was embedded in the concrete at the time that the concrete was poured, perhaps from a fire lit to keep the temperature of the curing concrete stable?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to P305 briefly -- pardon me. If we could have this introduced into evidence if it hasn't already. Is there a record -- I looked yesterday, and I didn't see it. I tender this as the next 1D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D197, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar, and if we can have P305 up just briefly. I apologise. I forgot this was the still photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a still photo from the video that we looked at yesterday that Mr. Groome tendered in his cross-examination, and I would ask you -- I would ask you to take a look at the same again, and tell me, do you see those lines in the concrete wall running horizontal?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have an explanation for those lines running horizontally?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be different levels. If I'm understanding you correctly, are you discussing, like, that line, then we have line here? It looks like it's different layers of concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the lines with a pen, perhaps a different colour pen than the red that was utilised in Mr. Groome's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before that's done -- do we have another copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Or do we have another copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that we use a different copy so that there's no confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now we have a clean photograph, sir. Could you please mark for us the horizontal lines that you talked about being different sections, different layers of the concrete.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Does that appear -- are you done, sir?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that appears to be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that -- do you have any opinion as to whether this wall was poured in one piece or whether it was poured in several sections?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be done multiple sections just based on the layers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked if there was a piece of wood stuck in the concrete. It's now gone to multiple layers expressing opinions about -- that this concrete was poured in multiple layers. There's been absolutely no foundation laid to establish how Mr. Dimas is able to look at this photograph and establish that it was poured in however many layers he's testifying it was poured in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you asked questions of the witness which were a little outside his expertise and an objection was raised, your answer was, He's here as an expert, and I propose to deal with this matter in the very same way. Let us hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to seeing now this empirical evidence that you believe that the walls were poured in sections, does that -- how does that affect your capability of excluding or including the possibility that wood used in a fire to heat the slabs while they were curing may have been embedded in the concrete during the building process?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very likely. Any time especially when you're mixing concrete for something to fall in, so that would make more sense since there is no practical purpose for that wood being in that concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this as the next 1D exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to focus on the wood beam that we had here, and while we're doing that, let's look at Y020-3614. And while we're waiting for that, sir, you examined the beam physically -- the piece of wood, I should say. You've examined it physically here in the courtroom. Did you note any evidence of charring or any evidence of fire or smoke damage or heat damage?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it showed no signs of fire damage whatsoever, no sooting, no charring, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, while we're waiting for the zoom to go in on the picture, looking at this photograph of that piece of wood in the wall, the photograph appears that there's no gap in it this time. Is this the condition that you saw the piece of wood at the time you performed your visual inspection physically at the premises?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Again, if you note if edge, the edge is smooth, even with the edges of the wall. The video also showed the left-hand side being flush with the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you -- I'm sorry, could you circle where you say the edge is smooth and it's in line with the wall, flush with the wall. If you could use that -- with the assistance of the court usher use a colour to circle that portion and label it 1.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what conclusions can you draw from the ends of the wood being flush on all edges?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that's how -- that's how I determined that it wasn't a furring strip. In addition, if it was used as a furring strip, you'd have boards attached and you'd see lines going upward, and had there been a separation, that would also be an indicator. I also looked at the dark area around, which was called in question as possible smoke damage, yet it doesn't -- you have it on top and bottom, yet it doesn't have any on the wood. So again, that is not a smoke pattern.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have this admitted as marked as the next available 1D exhibit number. I'd want to show two more photographs of this before asking the witness a question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D199.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, I'm going to ask to have two more photographs of this wood piece as you saw it on the scene shown to you: Y020-3615 and Y020-3613.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If they could be shown side by side, I think that would speed things up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, sir, do these two photographs depict the remainder of that piece of wood as it was on the site as you saw it in January of 2009?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, we viewed a video-tape produced by the Office of the Prosecutor from this weekend where this same piece of wood had some gap that was alleged or demonstrated. In your opinion, has something happened to this wood since the date that you inspected it?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, even on this one you can see some gaps where the concrete has actually fallen off around it, yet the edges are still intact, and they were intact at the time of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Great. If we could have these --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could mark those -- anything of interest to your description in this photograph, and then I would ask that they be tendered after the marking, and if you could describe for us what those markings mean.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the edges which we've just examined. Also, again, the cleanness of the wood. Depending on the size of the furring strips, we're not assuming that the wood finish -- if we're talking just wood planks, we'd say even if they were just smaller planks, we would see some type of lines where they once existed, yet we only see nails on this side of the board after we examine it here that there's maybe approximately three nails the full length, yet there's no edge next to those nails where a board would have been nailed to. So that's how I was able to eliminate anything being attached such as an exterior panelling. Also, as we discussed, this at one time was discussed as possible pattern, yet if it's the intention that that was involved in the fire and it's still there, we see no smoke damage to this beam itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, there was the hypothesis given by Mr. Groome that this is a furring strip and that the room had multiple furring strips that were taken down by somebody. Now, in watching the video-tape, we saw that a crowbar was required to take this piece of wood out of the wall and the wall deteriorated upon the wood being pulled out. The question I have for you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I'm not able to see what's being depicted in the video, certainly Mr. Ivetic shouldn't be able to talk about seeing wall crumbling when the piece of wood was removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I guess the video could be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It could, Your Honour, except that I don't have the numbers for the video, since, again, this was one that was disclosed to us last night, I have no way of playing it myself. It's on the Sanction system, which the Defence does not have access to, so ... if Mr. Van Hooydonk can locate the video in question and play it, that would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Defence will try to locate the video. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the interpretation in B/C/S are late, quite late because speakers are speaking quite fast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad the reprimand has come from you, Mr. Cepic, rather than me. You have to slow down, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, and I apologise to the translators and the Trial Chamber. Is it possible, Mr. Van Hooydonk?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, it's being called up now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are we going to lose the markings if we switch? I believe it was towards the middle of this clip, Mr. Van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Dimas, as we're all watching this video, when it comes time and the piece of wood is extracted from the wall, if you could please describe for us what your trained eye sees as to the wall and the material surrounding the wood as it being removed, that would greatly assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can clearly see when he first pulled it that some of the concrete actually started falling immediately. Again, when I reviewed that beam or piece of wood and excluded it as possible furring, I also examined the other walls, and that's when I found no indication that there was no other similar wood that would be used in that fashion. As I stated earlier, it wouldn't make sense that you'd put a finished section beneath one window inside your home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And one other question I have. The other -- the remaining walls that you observed in the basement room, did they appear to have been plastered over?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was evidence that they were a smooth plastered wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did it appear the smooth plastered wall had been painted?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't determine that. Portions were so badly decomposing, you could just tell smooth areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you expect to find a plastered wall with furring strips onto the plaster and then a wall finishing -- covering the plaster?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this marked exhibit -- marked photograph as the next 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D200, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the assistance of the court usher, I'd like to have this placed on the ELMO. This is the booklet that was used by the Office of the Prosecutor in the cross-examinations of Mr. McCoy and Mr. O'Donnell. I can't recall if it was used today or not, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We just saw the juncture box in this video that we heard some testimony about. Now, sir, you see this photograph which the Office of the Prosecutor has marked as being burnt timber in the wall pocket in the ground floor room.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What is that that we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's actually the electrical outlet and the area where the wiring went into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So the Prosecution's exhibit is misstating the empirical evidence from the site. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It's mis-marked. It's saying it's burnt timber, and they actually brought in that section today, and we were able to examine it. That is not timber at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, is it possible to take a screen-shot of this photograph and introduce it so we know which page we're dealing with or should I reference the page number? Because this was -- the whole booklet was introduced into evidence by Mr. Groome through Mr. O'Donnell. I don't have the book in front of me to know the page number, but -- oh, page 27. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated this piece was brought into the courtroom today. Again, with the assistance of the usher, if we could move the book aside and have the contents of bag C-1 brought to the witness. That's, I believe -- that I believe are the contents. Now, sir, are these the contents of the bag that was represented to you as being removed from that juncture box by Mr. Selsky during the Prosecution's mission this past weekend?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and -- except now it's labelled as the burnt electrical box.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, to your trained eye that has been to the site, seen other sites, is this material wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is this material concrete or plaster?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]

utterances.text: Is this material metal?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, are there any signs that you would expect to find on an exposed piece of concrete had the room been fully enveloped in a fire involving 60 to 70 persons who perished therein lasting for an extended period of time?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is there a possibility of tendering this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.text: Your Honour, they were all collected at the same time. Though I would agree to have them all admitted, I'm not willing to agree having them tendered piecemeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I stipulate, Your Honour. That's -- I think you should have all the pieces -- to have before you when making your decisions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the record's clear, so all of the evidence that this witness was shown today will be tendered into evidence. That includes eight exhibits, and I can -- after noon -- after we finish our session work with the Registrar to provide all the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit. Thank you. And while you're there, Madam Court Officer, can we get bag A-1 and the contents of bag A-1 ready for the ELMO; and, Mr. Van Hooydonk, if possible I'd like to have the video that I did mark down as 0930321, Pionirska, evidence wall, A-1 queued up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While this video is playing, sir, just for point of reference, do you recognise this dark line that we had the representation that bag A-1 is the charred wood from that black line?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's where they dug it out from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this appears to be a square that has a black line all the way around it, but there's concrete in the middle.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What is on the other side of this wall? What feature?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As you enter the room, this area is to the right of the entrance, the doorway.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, you're asking what's on the other side of that wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What's on the other side of the wall on the exterior of the home?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the area of the portico.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that also the area where a fire did occur, because we have the alligatoring wood on the portico?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Watch here. What was that piece of lighter material that just broke off from in front of the dark line and fell into the bag?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. If can you replay that one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could rewind it a little bit. A little bit more. A little more. Little more. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, that's part of the the wall, the concrete that he just busted off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree, or -- would you agree -- pardon me. Can you exclude the possibility that this line of wood was covered by concrete and/or plaster?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. For that matter, it could actually be the other side where the portico is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you exclude the possibility that the damage to this wood was caused by the fire on the portico that we know --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is clearly leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's your response to that as a leading question, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if it's -- I don't know. In my jurisdiction, it would not be leading. That's how expert witnesses are handled by both parties, but if Your Honours feel it's leading, I'll try to do it another way to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Given the knowledge you have of the location and the condition on the other side of this wall, what possible conclusions can you reach as to how this wood was damaged in the manner it was so damaged?

utterances.text: I cannot exclude that it was actually the burnt wood that was in that corner in the portico because that is the same area where the wood was on the other side, and especially having to break out the concrete like that, I can't rule out that that might not even -- that could be the exact same wood, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we earlier looked at some photographs of the upper level of this structure, and with respect to the timbers, why would timbers go through a wall?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, they support another level. It could be rafters that you -- a tier, say a light fixture. More than likely, it's for the support of a roof, things of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do we have any empirical evidence or can you reach any conclusions as to this particular wood that was the dark frame around that rectangular area, how far that extends to the outside?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This area that we just looked at where the contents of A-1 before you came from.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the thickness, size, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does it -- can you determine whether it extended all the way to the exterior where the portico was?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer will you be because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have the break, I know.

utterances.text: Right. Well, we'll take that I adjournment now, and we'll resume at 2.45 unless otherwise indicated. utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just two brief things. With respect to all these exhibits, to maintain the chain of custody, I'm going to instruct Investigator Selsky to re-bag them in new evidence envelopes, and we can sort out the mechanics of what the exhibits are this afternoon, if that's okay with Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I don't know what you were thinking about tomorrow, but since we're here, were you considering the morning schedule because we would -- oh, good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID

utterances.text: We will be resuming in courtroom II, and apologies, Your Honours. I understand bag C-1 has been admitted as Defence Exhibit 1D202.

utterances.text: We stand adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.06 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you are to continue and wind up your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Redirect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, me again. Now, you talked several times in the course of the cross-examination of Mr. Groome about a fully involved fire having to be approximately 1.000 degrees in a room. What effect would a fire of that magnitude have on the human body, that is to say on any people in a room? Let's take a hypothetical of there being 60 to 70 persons in a room? First of all, what effect would that presence of human tissue and human bodies have on the fire, and what effect would the fire have on the human bodies and human tissue, again, based upon your knowledge and experience?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: First off, human bodies, although they're considered people, in a fire they act as part of the fuel load, and as they're being burned they'll actually be part of the fire themselves, increasing temperatures due to their clothing, their skin, the body fat within a person. It all ads to the extent of the fire. And if somebody was to be in a fire of that degree, we'd see heavily burned bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would the presence of bodies as you say creating a fuel load for the fire, what effect would that have on the surrounding environment, that is to say the residue or deposits you would expect to find, wood, concrete, or other materials there?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would also add to the patterns as well. Again, they're basically incensed similar to a piece of wood. They're burning. They're giving off vapours, giving off soot. And they would add to the patterns you'd see, again, charring, sooting, patterns out the windows. Again, they're similar to a piece of wood being burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is that the phenomenon that is sometimes referred to as a dirty fire or flame?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about human bodies that would be collapsed on the floor-boards within the basement. Hypothetically speaking, if a fire reached a thousand degrees and fully enveloped that basement room, how would you expect the floor-boards throughout to be with respect to, again, the hypothetical, of 60 to 70 persons in that room perishing?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on how the bodies were laying on the floor, if they're stacked upon each other as they passed away, and how long the fire continued to be burned. If one body may be lying down with multiple bodies on top, there might be a protected area. However, if they continued to be burned, again, they're part of the fuel load, and everything would be consumed once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm waiting for the translation. Now, given this hypothetical, this hypothetical of 60 to 70 persons in a room of this size in a fully-evolved fire of a thousand degrees, do you consider -- or what would you say as to how long an observer or eye-witness to that fire could hear human cries for help, human screams in such a fire? How long does it take for the human body to succumb in a fire of that magnitude as is being offered by Mr. Groome's hypothetical?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, in most fires and with fire victims, it's not the burning that kills them. It's the smoke inhalation that they're breathing in. They'd succumb to that first, and then they'd perish. So usually while they're breathing, it could be a matter of minutes. I'd say 5 to 10 minutes, if not, 20 minutes, that they'd pass out because there's no oxygen for them to breathe. They're breathing in all products of combustion, and then they become burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, in a fully-enveloped fire, the entire room would be enveloped in flames of a thousand degrees; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Once the temperatures reach hot enough, the entire room would flash over, and that's a term when everything in the room becomes one total fire, and that's a fully-involved fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, there was at least one witness who claimed to have heard cries for up to an hour to an hour and a half while the fire was blazing. In your opinion, what can you say about that in regards to the hypothetical, a fully-evolved fire in that room?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be impossible in a fully engulfed room fire to have somebody alive that long. They would have perished, first off, like I said earlier, from smoke inhalation, and then the mere fact of the burns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just one more on that hypothetical. How -- what effect would the addition of accelerant, a combustible accelerant have on such a fire? Would it -- in terms of how quickly it would become fully evolved.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the fire itself, it would increase the quickness that it would go up to those temperatures, and the fire would reach those temperatures much faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as to the fate of any persons inside, how would the accelerant affect that?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By reaching those temperatures so much quicker, they would perish much faster as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to now have the contents of evidence bag F-1 available. Do we have that or not in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We do not have it. It's all been repackaged over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, with respect to bag F-1, sir, do you recall that was the piece of floorboard that was of a darkened colour, and I believe it had a knot in the middle, and you had it on the ELMO, and you appeared to be doing something to it before answering Mr. Groome's question as to whether there was evidence of charring or fire damage to this wood. What was it, sir, that you were doing with your hands to that piece of wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was feeling it for the consistency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the dark piece of wood is F-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Continue, sir. F-2.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was feeling it to see what it was like, if it was sooty, moisture content, to see if it reacted similar to any normal piece of burnt wood or charcoal-type wood would react. I was looking for the colours, the colour of the sooting when you're rubbing your fingers on it are more of a black. Where when you're dealing with something that's more moisture content, if you look at your hands when you're done, it's more of a brownish colour. It might be brownish grey, depending what's in it, where again the burnt wood or charcoaling would be black.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are those techniques ones that are trained for investigators of your type and utilised by investigators of your type?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. You use all your senses, so it's very important. That's why I got down hands on and examined it, and as I stated, I believe it was on my first day, that I actually physically snapped off a piece of the wood to examine it. It's a standard procedure for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so what I'm getting at is, did you also do those types of physical manipulation tests at the scene at the Pionirska location on January the, I believe, it was the 29th of this year?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With the assistance of the court usher, I'd like to have another one of the -- page 25 of the booklet of photographs produced by the -- tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor into evidence. I'd like to have that up on the screen. And while we're getting that set up, sir, I'm going to ask you about evidence bag A-5. If you recall, that was the piece of wood taken from the portico that Mr. Groome had you examine and turn over to talk about the phenomenon on the backside of the wood. And if you recall there was a piece of lighter-coloured wood jutting out from the side. And on the photograph that I'm not getting -- I apologise. On the top photograph, do you think you can locate that piece of wood in this photograph or the portion of this photograph that looks like that piece of wood?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The clean unburnt one? Is that what you're discussing?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That one right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let the record reflect, the witness is indicating the left centre of the -- left side towards the centre vertically of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, sir, having had the opportunity to review the backside of this piece of wood in court earlier today, can you give us a definitive answer as to whether this piece of light-coloured wood is a furring strip or not, given that it has been referred to as a furring strip by Mr. Groome with two witnesses -- actually, three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to P307, if we can have that pulled up. Sir, this was an exhibit that Mr. Groome had shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that the video by any chance? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately I've written down the exhibit number. I don't know the reference to give to Mr. Van Hooydonk to get off the Sanction, but let's stick with -- let me skip to -- if perhaps the Prosecution could try to locate that for me, I will stick with this photograph that we were talking about earlier. In the photograph that we just took off the ELMO, there were globules on the ceiling. I believe previously either you or one of the other witnesses may have referred to them as stalagtites. Given your physical examination of the premises, the inside of the room, do you have an opinion as to the moisture level in that room? Was there -- how would you describe the moisture level?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we're going well beyond anything that was raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the video I'm waiting for is the video as to the ceiling and the ripples in the ceiling that I'm right now asking about, so if it was beyond the scope of either cross-examination, then P307 should not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, certainly I think it's proper to ask questions about P307. And it's now prepared for viewing if Mr. Ivetic wants to show it again, but I don't ever remember asking my questions about stalagmites or stalactites or other things we find in caves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Stalagmites and stalactites were mentioned -- was that in examination-in-Chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm trying to get the LiveNote up so I can actually see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness did use that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was mentioned, I believe, in cross-examination when they were talking about water damage to the ceiling, is what my notes indicate, and I thought it was in relation to the video that was played, P307, when they were looking at the revealed rebar in the ceiling and talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll allow the question. Let's move on quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is the video now ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dimas, as we're playing the video again, I'd like to have you commentate as to what -- for those of us who are not in the room, what you see as to the ceiling and as to the particular any evidence of moisture causing the ceiling to deteriorate.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please articulate his words so that the interpreters can understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, and I think it was towards -- at least one-third into the tape, I think it was ceiling that was exposed. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What does the appearance of the surface of the ceiling indicate to you having been on the property as to the most probable cause for the ceiling deterioration that we see here?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was determined that it was due to severe moisture and water. The water while we were on site actually was physically dripping, and there were stalagtites coming down from the top. The moisture in that area, you could actually just reach up and touch it and feel that it was still dripping.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what about the discolouration that we see on the various portions of the ceiling as indicated in this video footage?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was moisture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.
