utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Van Hooydonk. I'm finished with that, and again, my great thanks for your assistance in that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about the door and the door frame. First of all, what can you tell us about the door frame? Was it affixed to the concrete wall in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared that it was just basically shoved in there, and that's one of the reasons why they needed the block, to also support it in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to -- let's put it this way. With respect to your overall totality of all the empirical evidence that you reviewed having been on the site, having looked at it, and now having had an opportunity to even review portions of that site brought here by the Office of the Prosecutor, has anything caused you to change your opinion from that set forth in your report as to whether or not this basement room was subjected to a fully evolved fire of the nature described by the Prosecution's witnesses in the statements that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: BENJAMIN DIMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only difference after reviewing the video from 2001, it actually more solidifies my findings due to the fact that there's no heavy sooting or charring -- or sooting above the windows and openings as their camera walked around. Again, that was 2001. That's way before I ever made it to the scene and much closer to the actual time frame that it occurred, so that helped out my findings. I really wish I would have had -- somebody looked inside. The other difference that I noted was, again, off the video, that was interior was being occupied by the bed frame and wood items in there, so, again, they may have had a fire after the fact. But as described by the witness statements I read, I found it totally inconsistent to have one to that degree. And now again after seeing the video that just helps me out more to solidify my findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dimas. On behalf of the Defence, I have no further questions in redirect, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your testimony. We thank you for coming to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I make one statement before I leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not part of our procedures.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence could call Prosecution expert Ewa Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had a discussion yesterday according to the schedule which I interpreted the Court's comments that we were going to abide by the schedule announced by Mr. Alarid on Friday which I had before me is Benjamin Dimas, Cliff Jenkins, Dr. George Hough, and possibly Vladimir Rasic. I'd ask that we -- if it wasn't clear, I ask the Court to correct me, and if it was clear that that was the Court's direction, I would ask that we follow that. Ms. Marcus is here, and she's prepared a cross-examination for Mr. Jenkins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is Mr. Jenkins here?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, he's not. He's being proofed as we speak, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I haven't --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's the Defence's prerogative --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- considering extenuating circumstances with the case. Two things have not been completed by this point, Your Honour. One of which is the testimony of Ewa Tabeau is necessary for the full evaluation by Mr. Jenkins. One of the responsibilities of a primary law enforcement officer would be to establish proof of death through whatever means necessary depending on the facts and circumstance of the case. In this particular instance, the Prosecution has sought to establish proof of death through two means; one eye-witness testimony which Mr. Jenkins is prepared to testify on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down. Would the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, the issue is much simpler. You put forward a certain order in which you're going to present your witnesses, and you have not followed that order. Yesterday the issue was raised by Mr. Groome, and the ruling that I gave was that you should maintain the sequence in that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the Court added Ewa Tabeau or permitted the addition of Ewa Tabeau just Friday, and considering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I know we have added it. The question is, when?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The situation is this, Your Honour. We either call back Mr. Jenkins in this rejoinder thing, which I'm not quite got a grasp of yet, or we get him in and out of here with all information available. Secondarily, Your Honour, to that is there's a final aspect of his investigation that he's not completed yet. And I'd actually ask the Court's assistance for that. Is we have set an interview time at the gaol tomorrow, Your Honour, at UNDU for 9.00 a.m. We have requested that Mr. Cliff Jenkins be able to attend that for purposes of inspecting Mr. Milan Lukic for identifying features consistent with the Interpol warrant that he was originally arrested under. That would be standard operating procedures for an arresting law enforcement officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just point out that Mr. Jenkins has been on the witness list since November.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we can only -- and we're fighting with OLAD to get him permission to go in because they think he needs a new background check in order to be permitted a visitor's pass into the gaol.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just with respect to this desire to have him examined -- Mr. Lukic's bodies [sic] for tattoos, I don't believe there's been any evidence introduced, the Interpol warrant has not been introduced in this case. I'm not sure what relevance Mr. Jenkins physical inspection of Mr. Lukic's body, how that assists the Court in any way with respect to the task it has before it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, it goes to the credibility -- one, it goes to the initial description given in the warrant which we would be tendering through the police officer investigator, which is that Mr. Milan Lukic originally was described as having moles and tattoos. And so these particular identifying features which is common for an arrest warrant, I can't have him come in and testify that Mr. Lukic is either consistent or inconsistent with that description unless he actually examines the body. And other than that, Your Honour, Ewa Tabeau's upstairs, and I don't understand why we're fighting over this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, it is true that Ms. Tabeau is upstairs. Why would you not be able to have somebody from your team? You are not lacking in resources, and her evidence is not new.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I will try to accommodate the Court, but it is difficult -- it's difficult to understand what happens between Friday and Tuesday that the schedule gets turned topsy-turvy, and I do not have unlimited resources. I allocate task in part in large reliance on what Mr. Alarid tells me is the order of the witnesses. Ms. Marcus is the person I've assigned to do both of those witnesses. If I could have a moment to ask her her level of preparedness on Ms. Tabeau, and if I can accommodate the Court, I will. But I would please ask Mr. Alarid if he is unsure about the schedule when he gives it Friday, please indicate that and tell us when he will be sure. But to tell us with certainty that certain things are going to happen Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and to come in Monday and say, I've changed it all, I just think it's discourteous and it's unfair to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's very trying. Very trying, Mr. Alarid. How long would it take you to get the officer who will be dealing with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe she's in the witness waiting room as we speak, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I'm asking Mr. Groome. How long would it take him to get the lawyer -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's Ms. Marcus who's doing both. And Ms. Marcus is prepared to start. I've asked Your Honours' indulgence. If she finds that there's something that comes up that she be given the opportunity if she needs some additional time, but I believe she's prepared to make a start on her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and with the Court's indulgence, we'll probably be using this a lot, so if we could just get P119 put on the screen, please, and we can start working with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may have one question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I know whose witness I am today because nobody actually told me for whom I'm testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Tabeau. If you recall, I'm Jason Alarid, and I represent Milan Lukic. We met sometime last year when you testified, and I hope all has been well with you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I am good, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I think we got in trouble last time for talking too fast because we're in the same language, so we probably need to observe a pause between testifying. And I want you to be organised, so you tell me when you feel comfortable with your materials.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I guess I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, just so I can ask you, I know that P119 was revised slightly with colour-coding, but the colour-coding didn't come in very well, and it actually obscured some of the writing because it's so small when you put that entire spreadsheet and then reduce it to 8 by 11 or the standard page size. Is that a blown-up version of your chart that have you in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I believe it is the P119. Not that I can be certain, but from the format I can see that -- yes. I have a printed copy that is far better, so at least I can read better. I'm not sure that anybody else can have the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, if I use the old version -- and, ma'am, if I use the old version, is there any significant difference between the old version and the new colour of coded one that's been attached to the most recent Prosecution motion?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is the same version, but this version should be read together with the clarification which for a number of records includes additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But did you actually change information on the chart other than adding colour?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No. The information remains the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So the clarifications in your report didn't necessarily change the chart but sought to clarify it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The clarifications in the report should be read together with the results in the P119.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I apologise. I mean, when we filed our motion, sometimes as lawyers we use strong words, and so I apologise for attacking your reports if I made you a little defensive in the reply, but there was no offense intended. So I hope you understand.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I say that, ma'am, is to be honest, I didn't really get the significance of your being part of this considering my naiveté with war crimes. And to be honest I thought you were just here originally to show this common scheme and practice, the large-scale, if you will, demographic and statistical evidence in the Visegrad area, and it kind of floored me when you ended up being also the -- sort of curator of the Proof of Death Project, if we can call it that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, is this an oral argument of some kind or an examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm trying to be nice, Your Honour, but I'm putting my case to her because I want her to know why I'm bringing her back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's have a question now, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your -- just to briefly re-iterate, you are an statistician; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what is the extent of your degree, if I might ask you to recall it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I have a Ph.D. in mathematical demography and a master's degree in economics with the area of statistics and econometrics.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that normally demographics and statistics would not be used in a proof of death scenario?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't understand what is normally and what is the proof of death scenario, normally -- normal proof of death scenario.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this. You call this the Lukic and Lukic Proof of Death Project; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When were you commissioned, if you will, to undertake an actual Proof of Death Project?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It was around the summer last year. I don't remember exactly the date. Sometime in June, perhaps a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If I may add, we are speaking about proof of death for Lukic and Lukic case, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because we are not generally speaking about proof of death practices as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me about the proof of death practices that you would otherwise understand.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, we've been engaged in these kind of activities for a long time. It dates back as far as the Srebrenica project started, so it would be sometime in 1999 or early in the year 2000. This is when these kind of activities were initiated. And since then we've been conducting this kind of analysis systematically for several cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why would it fall under your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because I'm in charge of the demographic unit and because I have been working a lot on victims issues, and that is the natural way why these things would be done by my unit and myself being involved in this, not to mention the fact that the Srebrenica project was conducted and completed in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But in terms of Srebrenica, how many people were we talking about?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In terms of victims, you mean, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, yes, potential victims.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is up to almost 8.000. This is the number of victims in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in the Srebrenica project, isn't it -- would it be fair that you weren't -- you didn't conduct that project with the goal of proving a death being tied to a specific culprit?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't understand exactly. If you can rephrase a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Here's why I'm confused, is, to me, when Mr. Lukic is accused of personally killing a specific person, and we'll just say plural, many people now, if you want to consider the list being a total accusation, as opposed to a general, who is accused of overseeing a large, chaotic, horrible thing of which some people might be involved, but that general didn't personally know or pull a trigger or -- in such a personal way. Mr. Lukic is accused of personally, first-hand being the culprit that kills these people in your list. And so my question is, how might it be different in Srebrenica than a small project such as this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honours, Dr. Tabeau is not an expert in the modes of liability or how the cases are proven. Dr. Tabeau has come to talk about the Proof of Death Project, so perhaps counsel could restrict his questions to areas in Dr. Tabeau's expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well -- and that's a very good point, Your Honour, because at the end of her testimony, we will be filing a motion -- we made the motion orally when she testified to strike as not relevant her report, and we will be renewing that motion at the end of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just ask her a question that's related to her expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So what about demographics? Other than having access to the data of census, of the Book of the Dead, of the International Red Cross reporting, what does trying to -- what does this Proof of Death Project for Lukic and Lukic have to do with demographics? You have access to the databases, but what does the actual project have to do with demographics?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, this is a very general question, but -- I actually don't know what do you want me to talk about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What he's asking is, how does demographics assist you in proving death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's actually a very useful question. The thing is that the knowledge demographers have about analysis of sources, data sources, being it victims or whatever other demographic events is very important because it gives us a broader perspective on how to analyse the sources, how to combine the sources, and how to read the results of our analysis. I wouldn't think that a statistician without a demographic background would be able to make the same analysis as we have done and have been doing for this project and many other projects. So the general experience, demographic experience that we have in data analysis, in the analysis of demographic processes, other processes such as birth or deaths or marriages or divorces, any demographic process, the same perspective can be applied in the analysis of data on victims. And this is something that others simply don't have. A statistician working on business data wouldn't be able to analyse data on demographic events including data on victims the way we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me see if I can assist, Mr. Alarid, further. Mr. Alarid is saying to you that his client is charged in this case with personally, physically doing particular things, killing particular people, let's say A, and he wants to know how those demographics assist you in establishing that Mr. Lukic killed A. Is that where you're leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. Part of it. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The answer is very simple. It is what we do goes beyond witness testimonies and witness statement, and we look at sources, which are often not used in legal proceedings, sources like the population census, sources on victims, sources on survivors. And by searching through these sources and integrating information such results from our work, we were able to provide additional information that either corroborates or rejects the statements made by the witnesses. So it's a very useful approach which I think is quite exceptional, and I don't think it is an approach that can be thought of in many places of the world. From this point of view, this Tribunal is very lucky, having all these sources and people who have the demographic expertise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think I might have misstated the proposition. It's not how does demographics assist you in establishing that Mr. Lukic killed A, but how does demographics assist you in establishing that A was killed? I think that's putting it more accurately because the Prosecution would have adduced other evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- as to Mr. Lukic's alleged responsibility for killing A. It is how does demographics assist you in establishing death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As Your Honours already stated, we can't help establish whether Mr. Lukic killed these people or not. We can help establish whether these people were killed or survived by using our sources and our expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But wouldn't it be fair to say that that has nothing to do with statistics?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I disagree. It has all to do with statistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. In your clarification, you put two numbers by ratio, and I understand ratio, of consistencies between the list of the names and reported census data on one hand, International Red Cross data on another hand, and Book of the Dead data. And you put -- and you put some numbers. Can you tell the numbers. What is the ratio -- without stating specific victims or alleged victims, rather, what is the ratio of alleged victims that also have corresponding biographical data per the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It's all in the clarification. When we are speaking of 86 names of victims from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Schedules, yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- schedules. And as far as I remember the ratio was about 69 per cent, that many names were confirmed in the census approximately, if I'm right. But if you want correct figures, it is all in the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before you did this and as you correlated your evidence, did you consider at all what is legally required under Yugoslavia's laws to establish proof of death?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, not really. Not really indeed. I've never spoken in my clarification or any other report about legal standards in the former Yugoslavia for proof of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, might death records from a country actually be an additional data set that might assist you in conducting a complete investigation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Oh, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, those two questions are quite directly leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I beat around the bush --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Don't lead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll try not to, but for foundational purposes, Your Honour, I don't want to just beat around the bush and waste too much of the Court's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you have called her as your witness, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would ordinary standardised Yugoslavian proof of death records assist you in collaborating the information, or corroborating is a better word, the information in your report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what is an ordinary standardised Yugoslavian proof of death record? I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Death certificates. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, put that, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you do a search of any death certificates?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, we used two huge databases, the so-called DEM 2 databases. One of the federal authorities, statistical authority, and one of the RS authority. Altogether, these two databases contain approximately 140.000 death records. A large number of them are documented by death certificates, regular Yugoslav, or say, Bosnian standard death certificates. Many are not, but it is that we searched in this kind of information, in this project as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, what is the total number of deaths we have in our sub-set here?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In the sub-set of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Of our victims.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of our victims. The number of listed victims from the indictment is 86 for these two incidents, right, Pionirska and Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. And of the 86, how many were you able to establish by formal death records?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, in RS mortality database, the DEM 2 database, none; and in the federal statistical authority, as far as I remember, 9 or less. But we are speaking of known deaths. In these databases, there are known deaths included, no missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But missing persons doesn't necessarily tell you how, when, or where someone died.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Missing persons are missing, so there is no account of how the person died, where the person died, what was the cause of death. They are reported missing. There is no body found yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what significance do you attribute to not being placed on the missing persons list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is an important issue. It is not -- the ICRC list of missing persons is exhaustive. It is not that every missing person who ever went missing in the territory of Bosnia or other countries of the former Yugoslavia is reported in the ICRC records. But there are other lists of missing persons, and there is no one-to-one correspondence between the ICRC list and other lists. We use the ICRC list, not the other list. So it is possible that a number of missing persons are not on the ICRC list at all. They might be on other lists. They might be not reported anywhere at all. It is also possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true, though, that death certificates and decisions of death by a Court are not at statistical offices but in the books at other governmental agencies?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is very leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Where are death certificates and decisions of death kept in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There is that obligation of notifying the statistical authority of a death, so if anybody dies, then within three days the family has the obligation to notify the authority about this death. And the death is registered then in the vital statistics office, and together with the death certificate, I believe the record of death is kept in these local offices. It is different now in the war-time for obvious reasons, of course. Not all -- many local vital statistics offices didn't operate properly, so a lot of these death notifications were not submitted and were not kept, not archived. So there are, though, these two central databases, one RS, one federal statistical authority database, which collected whatever was available.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was from these databases that you confirmed the nine?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And did anything about those nine tell you the when, where, and how they perished?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For whatever record was found, there is a date of death, place of death, and possibly a cause of death. However, we are speaking of cases, death cases of missing persons. In exceptional circumstances, these kinds of notifications were accepted, and this was in cases where there were court decisions available, local courts or cantonal, regional courts in Bosnia-Herzegovina that declared certain individuals dead. These declarations were issued based on witness testimonies. There was a requirement of at least two witnesses, eyewitnesses to testify in order to -- that such declaration could be issued. So even if these nine cases or six - I don't remember exactly the number - for these cases, I wouldn't think death certificates available. It is likely that these cases were registered based on court declarations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, did you consider the -- what was your original sub-set of victims? Was it strictly from the indictment, or did you tabulate any information from the actual witness statements of your own -- with your own due diligence and error-checking?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We received a list of victims from the Lukic and Lukic Prosecution team. We checked, compared this list with the list of victims from the indictment. There were a few differences, like, for instance, one person was listed twice; I'm speaking of Hasan Kurspahic. And in addition to this list we explicitly requested and received from the team information about the relatives of these victims. So for every victim, we had the names and the approximate age as reported in the indictment, and in addition to this, we received information about the relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the accuracy of your report somewhat reflects on the accuracy of the information given to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Does the accuracy of your report, or can the accuracy of your report reflect upon the accuracy or inaccuracy of the information given to you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of course the input information is very important. If there are errors in the input information, it is unlikely that there will be no errors in the outcomes. But what we always do, we double-check. So I ask a colleague of mine to go through witness statements and check the information on relatives provided and correct any mistakes in the names or insert additional names, so that we would work with a full and correct information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who is this colleague?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is Mr. Beecham. He's a member of my unit, and he's specialised in searches in our archive of witness statements and other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I ask you that is in the clarification, there are some footnoting that appears that there was some, you know, secondary verification work done. And so I was wondering, who did the secondary verification work as noted in the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by secondary verification, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. I can give you an example on the front page here. I'd like to you look at number 3 particularly, Hasan Kustura, listed as one of the five victims of the Drina River incident.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You are speaking of P119; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. And it should be on the screen --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers, kindly not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay ... now, of course Mr. Kustura, as you listed him in the summer of 2008 appeared to be alive.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is what you can read from P119, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, it's -- because -- I'm just looking at this, and you have that he voted in 1998.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The person who voted was Hasan Kustura, father's name, Ahmet, born on the 7th of May, 1939. That person is registered as a voter in 97, 8 elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, with you maybe only having maybe the name of Hasan Kustura, how did this person's personal data end up on P119?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In several cases, there were several alternative matches to the names on the schedules, so Hasan Kustura was one of these names, and if you go to the clarification --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to that in a second --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, counsel continually cuts off Dr. Tabeau and she's not able to finish her explanation. If you want her testimony, I would submit that she should be allowed to finish her answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speak, kindly not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you finish the last answer, rather.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started speaking about alternative matches. And what is seen in this current version of P119 are one-to-one matches. No alternatives are shown. Certain choices were made to simplify the outcome of our analysis. In the case of Hasan Kustura, the most conservative choice was made, which means we are showing a person who is registered as a voter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This person is listed here with place of residence in Visegrad. This is how the person is reported in the census. It doesn't mean this is the only match we obtained for this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before we get too far afield, please, for the record, can you tell me what names in P119 you have for -- what death certificates you have or declarations of death do you have for the victims listed in P119.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, we just discussed the issue, and the conclusion was that these persons are missing persons, and the expectation of them being reported as known deaths in them two databases is wrong. So this is why you can't see cases in P119 which would be documented by death certificates. There will be a few documented, for instance, by missing persons, ICRC missing persons records.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, but, ma'am, I'm just asking you -- I think you said you had nine.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please remember to pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am sorry. I'm sorry. From the federal statistical authority, them two databases, we obtained in total ten matches within P119. Unfortunately, the matches are not listed because you only -- them two database included in P119 is RS mortality database, RS DEM 2 database. And with this database no matches were obtained. There is a footnote, however, in the report in which I explain the matches obtained from the federal authority database, and this is footnote 8 on page -- on page 8 of the English version of the report. So for the Pionirska --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Pionirska, you found how many links?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Six out of nine. Six. Six. This is the number for the Pionirska victims in the DEM 2 database of the federal statistical authority. That would be the cases that you are saying are possibly documented with death certificates. And I'm saying not necessarily, because even when registered in these kind of databases, the death certificates might very well not be available because these are cases of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What is the statistical significance of six out of the total number of listed Pionirska Street victims?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It's of course not a large number, as we know, but if you are saying that the existence of a death certificate is the ultimate proof of death, then I must say in what circumstances? In normal, peace-time, maybe very well so, but we are speaking about a conflict, a time when there's a chaotic situation where offices don't work normally, where people are on move, and many things are happening parallel at exactly the same time. So you cannot expect that death cases from the conflict will be documented exactly the same way as death cases in the peace-time. That is simply not the case. It's not the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know the requirements if missing what is required by a court to establish death and issue a death certificate in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I already told you that I didn't study this issue, and I don't know the legal requirements for the proof of death in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what is the statistical significance of one of five people on your list being alive, for the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What five people? What five people? Have you to explain first why five people are alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Excuse me. There's five people listed for Drina River on page -- at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And one of those five is alive.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Well, I wouldn't dare to calculate any percentages because this is really a very small sample.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How about 20 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I disagree. This is just five persons, you know. Just live it out. Calculating percentages doesn't make sense here at all. And on the other hand, I must tell that you this is misleading to insist that Mr. Kustura, the one listed here is the victim from the indictment, because the other half of the story is that there was another Hasan Kustura.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: And this one was the victim, not the one listed here conservatively as a potential survivor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You realise this Hasan Kustura just asked for his property back?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't know that. You know more than me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, how many alternative matches did you have specifically with regards to Mr. Kustura?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, objection. I think Dr. Tabeau has still not been able to finish her explanation. She's being cut off consistently, so I would respectfully request the Chamber to ask Mr. Alarid to please allow Dr. Tabeau to finish her answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you have more to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just wanted to say we had two matches of Hasan Kustura. And the second match was studied recently very thoroughly using the census data and links between the families and familial relationships. And based on our study, we had a theory that actually the person included in P119 is the wrong match, is a mismatch, and that the other Hasan, with father Ibrahim, born in 1959 is the right person and should have been included in P119 instead of the person conservatively chosen in September last year. And farther, there were investigations run by the Prosecution team which we didn't -- were not involved in these investigations, but people were contacted; people were interviewed down in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And we were collecting all the results of these investigations in order to be sure whether the results of our searches are corroborated by the results of independent investigation by the team. And at some point we received confirmation that the record we actually declared recently as the right match was exactly the same as the result of the investigation by the Prosecution team. And I'm speaking about this way of working in the clarification. The ultimate goal of this clarification is checking the uncertainties around a number of victims claimed to be survivors using all possible information sources that we have here at our disposal in my unit but also using the results of investigations that they were supposed to do. This is their responsibility to talk to people, to contact people and clarify the issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't that the injection of a potentially subjective set of information?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't understand why subjective. If you think of, you know, any information that we've been working with, anything is subjective. Victim names come from witnesses. It's subjective. Relatives come from witness statements. It's subjective. What is not subjective are the sources we have. The census is not subjective --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The OTP's not subjective?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The OTP's not subjective --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's a question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, it is -- I'm speaking here about my work and not about my employer. I'm here as a statistician and as a demographer. I can tell you everything about my work, about the sources I use, about the methods I use, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so one of those sources is OTP investigation information; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, as I said, my work is demographics. I work with well-established official sources. One of the sources is the population census. There is another set of sources, and these are sources on survivors, voters registered for the 1997, 1998, and 2000 elections. There is a register of internally displaced persons and refugees. And there are many sources on victims that I have in my unit, and this is the material with which I work, and this is all objective. And the method I use is objective and expertise I have is objective. I have no more examples right now, but in my view it is all very objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But that's because a statistician shouldn't be subjective. Statistics with all hope are a neutral determination.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: These are all general, you know, things, whether statistics is subjective or objective. I think we are speaking here about a very concrete project, a project in which our task was to verify a number of names in the census, and starting from there, to check whether individuals reported in the census were also reported in other sources, both, on survivors and on death or missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What prompted you to investigate or reconsider number 4, Hasan -- or number 3, rather, Hasan Kustura?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, you, actually in your motions there, because you raise this issue of alleged survivors, so intensively in such a large scale that actually we found there is a need to double-check the results of our work that we completed in September, and by looking at the survivors alleged in your motion, we thought it's also important to take another look at the survivors that -- potential survivors that we identified already back in September last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So who confirmed with VG-32?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You need a name of an investigator or an OTP? What -- what is the question about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't remember the exact name. If you need me, I will check it in my e-mails. I have it all documented, so if it's so important for you to know the name, I will check it and I will come back to you with the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you also for the entire list of victims, can you provide me with the alternative that you at least considered as potentials when you were first compiling the list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The alternative matches?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, you already have quite a number of them, and you don't realise that. It is all in the clarification in the Annex A. There are a lot of tables which actually respond to this question. These are the alternative matches, you know, by proving that certain individuals you alleged to be survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, exactly, ma'am, but I didn't allege all of them to be survivors, and it sounded to me like you found on your own alternative matches before I ever raised the question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If you want to -- if you are really interested in studying this, I can provide this. That's not an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please do that, ma'am. I'm very interested.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I will write it down. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where are we going with this, Mr. Alarid, because -- how long do you plan to be in your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I can see taking the -- not the whole session but enough time hopefully to finish Ms. Tabeau full and final today is what I'm -- my goal is. I have about -- I have about 45 more minutes of questioning, but with the breaks and stuff, you know, wherever that takes us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are going to take the break at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, with the Court's -- usher's assistance, can we use the pen, please, the screen pen. Now, I'd like you to put an X through Hasan Kustura, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In what field?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Over his name.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, are there any other -- on the first page, page 1 of 16, any other persons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is misleading because counsel has not referred to the entirety of the entry, and if we turn to the end of the entry we will see the alternative Hasan Kustura is listed in P119 at the end of that line. I haven't said so until now, but now that we are marking something which is only a portion of that entry, I feel it is highly misleading to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But we have all the evidence in front of us, but I don't think it's misleading, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may add --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- there is part of the screen which is hidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, part of the screen is hidden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And that is the important part that is hidden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is the important part. Can we get that on the screen, then, the part that is hidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It would be on page 9 of 16, ERN number 0641-6049.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But it all depends on what the X indicates, and we haven't been given any -- [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe from the clarification, Your Honour, Mr. Kustura was originally listed as the victim, and we're taking him off. That's what the X --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must object.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because if you look at the portion of the information on the screen, then you are seeing the record of the other Hasan Kustura with father Ibrahim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. And just -- let's discuss that for a second. Tell us about your qualification, rather, or limitations of the Book of Dead in your work.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In the -- you want me to speak about the Bosnian Book of Dead, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am, because here's my situation here, is -- well, maybe just -- you'll answer this, and I'll go away on it. Do you have a JMBG number for Hasan Kustura, son of Ibrahim?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is not, though, in this P119.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why wouldn't you include that in this since that is relevant information that shows the person at least was in the system?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I just explained that the choice of match with the census was conservative. The potential survivor was shown, not the other Hasan Kustura with father Ibrahim born in 1959. So this is the only reason where that JMBG is not listed. Otherwise, if both these matches were included, and I should have done this rather than picking up just one of the matches.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why did you originally pick one over the other before the clarification?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, the purpose was to simplify things. With alternative matches, the spreadsheet is far bigger than what it is now, right? But obviously, my subjective decision, I was the person who was editing the spreadsheet and preparing the final version of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I say that is, is because it seems illogical to me that you would have picked the first Hasan because, one, he voted; and two, there was no missing person report for him that would have otherwise piqued your interest; and three, there's another guy that's at least listed in the Book of Dead, and so why pick the other guy?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, there is a rule, golden rule that we have. We've been conservative always, always in our work. So if there is an evidence as in this case that a person possibly wasn't a victim but survivor, then I am showing this. This is this reason why, but I learned if this experience. Next time I will do it. I will include all alternative matches, disregarding how complicated it is for you, for the Defence, for the Prosecution, and for the Chamber. But the thing is that these subjects are complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Here is where I'm confused: What is conservative about naming Hasan Kustura number 1? Why is that the conservative choice?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because he's a registered voter, so there is evidence that possibly and likely he survived. This is why I'm showing this, and -- well, simplifying your task, actually, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that because I don't know where the other gentleman was registered. You know, was he registered in that part of the country or the opposite side of the country? Those are the kind of things that I would be interested in knowing, because proximity of the crime also is one of the factors I would consider.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The other person is from the Visegrad, so it is not that the other person is completely, totally out of the sky. So whatever information you need might be provided to you. What more can I say? I hope I answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Kind of. Thank you. Now, with regards to the Varda allegations, what concerns me there is that you listed several individuals that say Varda uncharged.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. There are such names in P119.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why did you include names that were not in the indictment as part of this data set?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Actually, I don't know why. This is probably because I had these names in the file sent to me by the Prosecution, so this is why. I just completed the searches, or we completed the searches for all individuals listed in the Prosecution files.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did any of these other people have indicia of being alive as opposed to dead?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't understand the question there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, see, we don't have the usual person identifying the body or the autopsy and all the other safe guards that normally tell us we got the right person. And so I understand what you're trying to do, and I'm just trying to get as much of a grasp on it as I can. To me, there seems like there would be three types of people, one that you know are alive, one that you know are dead, and one that is a question mark, one way or another, that you as a statistician shouldn't comment on.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is a very black and white picture, sir, you are drawing here. This P119 is no more than an overview of related sources of information. I don't draw any conclusions in the P119 as to whether the persons on this list are dead or alive or inconclusive whatsoever. There are no conclusions. This is just an overview of search results, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it's not a demographic study?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In what sense, demographic study? You have some statistics in the clarification from P119, some statistics about how many were found in the census, how many were found in the ICRC, how many were found in other sources. So in this sense, there were some statistics, but in P119 there is no study as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would you consider a 69 per cent reliability factor a strong coefficient of reliability or a weak one?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You are speaking of the matching rate with the population census, the 69 per cent, but the best matching rate we ever obtained is 87 per cent, and this is for the Srebrenica list. So compared with this, it's relatively low, indeed, but the information -- the input information is not very rich, too, so this is the explanation why.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, to be honest it shocks me because the fact that you find 87 per cent reliability on such an 8.000-person population like Srebrenica and you only have a 69 per cent reliability with direct family identification, meaning the information on the persons came straight from eye-witness family members; no one's guessing, is my point. And so what I put to you, ma'am, is this, is of the 16 -- of the 31 per cent that have no corresponding biographical data, can we consider them non-persons?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, absolutely no. This is the concept of this fictitious persons which comes back now and then on several occasions, in this case, other cases. Why one should believe that if there is no match with the census the person never existed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because if I say my mom's name is Susan, I expect you can go to the county clerk and verify her, and so these are names given by family members. There should be no confusion. That's my point.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right. But if you go with the name Susan and ask for confirmation of your mom Susan, believe me, you wouldn't receive one record. You would receive hundreds of thousands of Susan's wherever you live, in the United States, Mexico, whatever. That is an important issue of input that you provide, you know, so the families --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, I guess I'm -- this is -- it appears to me that on 31 per cent of your data set, you had no date of birth or JMBG number or IRC reporting or anything that corresponded to a real live person that you could include and say you verified. Isn't that fair?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You forgot that you have all these individuals, all of them from the indictment, witness statements. It is something that cannot be neglected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So is the why a question or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think it is an important piece of information. It is not perfect because witnesses done have perfect memory. They forget dates. They misspell names. So there is a lot of problems in their reporting, but it doesn't mean that these victims never existed. These are two completely different issues. If we speak of errors, yes. Errors are everywhere. In every source that is related to victims of war, there will be errors, whether this source is coming from the witness statements or is coming from organisation like BBD, Bosnian Book of Dead, or whatever else, there will be errors, but it doesn't mean that the war never happened and people were never killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, for your purposes, for the people that you have no data, what information that you have that they really ever existed?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I have names and relatives and approximate age. It is most certainly not nothing. I believe as an input and for my work, it is a good beginning. Of course it is not the same as in ICRC records, where I have far more information than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you aware of reparations and benefits in Bosnia for killed members of one's family?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You mean financial compensation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I've heard of several projects, of course, but if you ask me to give a concrete example of what projects run by whom with what mandate, et cetera, I wouldn't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Might -- did you consider the potential for financial gain as an impetus for over-reporting or fictitious names?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, sir, I have no experience with this kind of road. I must say, I can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you didn't?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I said I can't answer because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we go to page --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So, ma'am, would it be fair to say, though, that we can leave Ibrahim Hasan Kustura on the list, but we would be able to put an X through the gentleman that voted in 1998?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So the X would have to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Eliminating him as a potential victim.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yeah, but you asked me to cross the victim from the indictment. That is wrong. The other field should be crossed in the P119. We have to be very, very strict here, sir, because this spreadsheet, this one spreadsheet contains references and links to very many different sources. So you really have to be careful what you are crossing. The cross, yes, but not where I made it, in a different cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you consider people that were listed twice by virtue of their maiden name and their married name?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not that I recall in the context of Lukic and Lukic project.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that there were two individual women on this list that were both listed under their Kurspahic name as well as their other name, would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, there are no surprises. Everything can be explained. You give me their names and other details; I will check and come back to you with my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you consider that every person that might not have a corresponding Book of the Dead reference and/or ICRC reporting might simply be alive and somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, these are simplifications and conclusions that may not be drawn, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to put on the record that this is truly a cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We'd be here forever, Your Honour, if I didn't focus her somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We went through that, Ms. Marcus, with another witness called by Mr. Alarid. And I know that in the system from which you come and from which I come, you can't cross-examine your own witness unless the witness is hostile. But I did conclude that I thought it was appropriate in the context in which the Tribunal finds itself to relax that rule a little, and I didn't want to rehash the entire argument, argumentation, so I've been giving Mr. Alarid a little leeway. So Mr. Alarid, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have ERN number 0641-6042, please. Next page, I believe, from ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, who I'm going to focus your attention on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps the doctor anticipated this when she asked at the beginning, for whom was she being called? For which party? And I gave the answer, the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to focus your attention first on the Jasarevic family. Reference is 21, 22, 23, and 24. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I don't think we have to go backwards on the e-court, but in looking at your own list on page 10 of 16 of your same list, do you see that there's no BBD references for these same four individuals?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What significance is it that there is no corresponding census, ICRC, or BBD information related to these specific names?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This only means that we didn't find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is the other alternative that they never existed?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I must strongly disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Why? Because the theory of fictitious persons has never convinced me in any circumstances, not in this case and not in other cases. There are errors in data sources as I said. Errors. Misspelled names. Wrong dates. Incomplete dates. So finding a record is not easy. It's very hard to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You -- I think we covered this the last time you were here. You covered the 1991 census, but did you cover any other censuses, compare and contrast; i.e., a reference from a previous census is carried over in the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, we have been working with 1991 census and not with other -- any other censuses from the former Yugoslavia, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The reason I ask you this is that the people referenced are 49, 47, 42, and 35. Might they be of an age that you might be able to get statistical reliability from using an earlier census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If we perhaps -- you are referring to the numbers in the P119, 49, 47 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: As their ages. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So what is it? These are the records that you mentioned previously, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's in your -- it's in your column, L and L year of birth. There's no references. Then L and L age, approximate.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right. So what's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question is, is would it be useful to check earlier data sets such as earlier censuses to see if there's a corresponding reference to someone with this name, with this approximate age in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The age indicates that they should be included in other censuses, earlier censuses. However, this censuses are not available electronically as is the 1991 census, and I don't have the censuses on paper in my archive. So it would require contacting the authorities in the former Yugoslavia, although I'm not sure whether the names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I didn't mean the interrupt the answer, but am I correct in saying that the Court wanted to take a break at 4.15?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before we take the break, some of the source material for Dr. Hough is coming in. This is the first batch. It looks dick like -- second batch. It says volume 2. It looks like about 500 to a thousand pages. He's scheduled to be called tomorrow. Can I get an estimate of exactly how much source material we're going to receive today? I'm just wondering if it is physically possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I didn't want to overwhelm you, but I didn't want to leave anything out. Some of that's the witness statements that we had already line-itemed out. The only stuff that's going to be new that you don't already have is actual Articles that he may or may not refer to as well as his personal notes and the test result data that you required. And that's small in comparison, but I didn't want you to say that I didn't give you anything that might be relevant for your purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Will the personal notes and test data be -- will that be clearly identified because it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Hand-written. It's going to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm overwhelmed at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That's the one, but I didn't think that was the one that was going to hurt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I finish?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you were answering, and then we'll take the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was going to speak about the names. The statistical authority don't work with names, so the names are usually separated from other items collected during the census. And I believe it would be hard to trace these individuals in censuses earlier than 1991. That's because of this standard practice of the statistical authorities in the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take the break now, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to get off this first page, so let me refer to you a couple things and have you comment on them before we move on. Number 19 on your list -- and just to be clear, in the field for Lukic and Lukic case and then the number system, it's larger than the total list as part of the annexes in the indictment, isn't it? You have more people listed in your spreadsheet than are actually in the indictment; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, because of the chart, for instance, and Hasan Kurspahic listed twice, it's more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, specifically with number 19, Jasmina Delija, she has corresponding national data, and it appears that she is both listed as missing in the International Red Cross and is listed in the Book of Dead, so this is one of those people that we have total confirmation for; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But I would like you to look at Mina Kurspahic. And I believe that's on -- excuse me. Yeah, number 59 on page 5 of 16. Now, just looking at the first page, Jasmina Delija, it says her mother is Bisera.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it appears Mina has the same mother. Can we just eliminate the maiden name from your list based on this cross-referencing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, sir, I would need more information to say that this is the same person listed twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If testimony has been presented under oath to that fact, would you agree that the maiden name should not be included if the most current name is married?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of what two cases are we talking? Because we --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Jasmina Delija --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- and Mina Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You are saying this is one and the same person?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, based on the mother's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Based on the mother's name, and that Jasmina -- Mina is short for Jasmina. And sworn testimony presented in court.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I am unaware of this testimony. This is one thing, and in order to confirm that this is one and the same person, I would need more information from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true, though, that the Mina reference that has no corresponding national data, ICRC, or Book of Dead?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, there is no ICRC record. Is that correct. But there is BBD case ID included.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's interesting.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because who would do that? Who reports -- fills the Book of Dead?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Who fills the Book of Dead? The people who work on this project, on the Book of Dead, right? But I can explain you the case where IDs are included, record IDs from BBD and no further information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Okay. So the thing is that if you look at the BBD record of this person, it's exactly the same as the record in the indictment, so in such cases meaning that it says it is Mina --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- Kurspahic, born in 1972.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Which is calculated backwards, 1992 minus the approximate age, and that the person is reported as killed in this case in BBD in Visegrad on 14th of June, 1992. So that is a case that is perfectly consistent with the indictment victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause for the translation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please explain why none of that corresponding similar information is listed in the table.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because in such cases with the information identical in the indictment and in BBD, we expected that BBD record was taken based on the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If you know, are you aware of how the final list as annexed in the indictment came about? Do you have some information, hearsay or otherwise, that gives you an idea as to how the final tally came about?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, the final list from the indictment, how this list was made, you're asking whether I know? I don't know the detail. I do know that the lists were compiled based on witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, thinking -- let's just say hypothetically that four witnesses with differing people, let's say some might remember 15, some might remember 50, but regardless of that fact different people -- there are differences between the names listed from four separate witnesses. Would the proper way to assess the final list be an all-inclusive or one that's rather where witnesses actually corroborate each other, i.e., saying the same name?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, sir, it is known fact that witnesses don't remember all details correctly. They wouldn't remember all victims, probably, so I wouldn't say the list is all exhaustive. I don't think so. There will be problems in the list made based on witness statements and witness testimonies, even sworn testimonies, because people are imperfect. They honestly and truly will tell you about things they remember, but it doesn't mean that the things they remember are 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I think we concluded a little earlier that the witness identification part of it is the most subjective side of your analysis or at least subjective data set?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. That misstates the evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please clarify if I've misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, how do you say it misstates the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau never confirmed. It was no a question from Mr. Alarid, if I'm not mistaken. Dr. Tabeau never confirmed that this was actually subjective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct, Mr. Alarid. Reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. Is it significant to your analysis that the most exhaustive list, the most similar to the indictment was compiled with someone illiterate, VG-13, and it was done by a read-back?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I am not aware of VG-13 and illiteracy of this person and whether the person compiled a list or not, so I can't answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You're an expert, so you're allowed to answer things based on a hypothetical. So assuming that to be true, is that significant to your analysis?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
