utterances.text: Well, what is significant for my analysis is the information that I receive to be checked, disregarding the source the information comes from, and what is relevant and significant for my analysis, how I checked this information, what sources I used for cross-referencing this information, and to what extent I can corroborate or reject the details provided me in the input data for my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What significance is it when the -- let's the ICRC date of disappearance disputes the date of the crime alleged in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the date of disappearance is the date the person reporting to the ICRC, so the victim, the missing person last time, so it is perfectly possible that this data is inconsistent with the date of actual death of the actual incident. This is one thing. Of course, one would expect some degree of consistency, so the date of last seen shouldn't be later than the date of actual death if the date is known.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just that point's going to jump out at us, and so let's just get it out of the way. Ismeta Kurspahic who is referenced on page, I believe, 4. She's number 49 on page 4 of 16 of P119. If we have sworn testimony in court that says that there was only one Ismeta, and this is a hypothetical, if there's only one Ismeta in Visegrad, period, and that the age of that victim is consistent with the biographical data that you have, so there's some consistency there, but that person Ismeta is registered in the -- or an Ismeta rather, I think, because you address this in your clarification, is seen being admitted in the Visegrad health centre on June 18th, 1992, is that significant to your assessment?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is not because the person whose in the sworn testimony said there was just one Ismeta this age in Visegrad might be very well wrong. What is objective and what is my source to check this information is the census data.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you have any other Ismetas as part -- because you're going --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers not overlap, kindly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because you're going to get me everywhere there was another or a matching name, was there any other for Ismeta?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I suggest -- I take you to page 17 of my clarification where the case of Ismeta Kurspahic is discussed. It is number 49 in P119. It's page 17 in the clarification, last paragraph at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, and tell the Court your findings, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So this paragraph, the next page, page 18, this paragraph continues, so that is a discussion of this case. So my comment on the hospital admission record, it's a very poor record. There is no age. There is no date of birth. There is no place of residence. There is first name and surname in the record. You included a copy of this record, hospital admission record of Ismeta in your motion, so we studied this record. So there is nothing about age in this record. This is first of all. Second, in the census data, two different persons were found with the first name Ismeta and family name Kurspahic. Very different persons with different dates of birth. So the one that was born in 1960, for this person there is no evidence that she survived the conflict other than your hospital admission record that you claim is of this particular victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Actually, ma'am, I'm not claiming she survived the conflict. I'm simply saying she was alive on the day after the fire in Pionirska.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, what -- sir, what I'm trying to say, first of all, if a witness in a sworn testimony claims that there was this one person, just one person with this first name and surname, living in Visegrad area, I'm saying the witness can be very well wrong. And my task is to check whether there were other persons with the same names, and I can do this because I have the source, and I have the tools, and I have the expertise, and this is what I have been doing. And by studying the candidate records from the census, I can narrow down my search results, and I can drop the candidates that seem to be completely irrelevant, and I can focus on the candidate which fits the profile of the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But if additional information comes in, i.e., from an extra source such as a hospital record and there's nothing else to dispute that, is it possible that Ismeta Kurspahic was alive on the 18th of June, 1992, and whether she lived a day past that, we don't know, but for all you know it's the same Ismeta as is part of the list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What I'm saying, there were more than one Ismeta Kurspahic, and what I'm saying, is hospital admission record is poor, and I can't use this record. I can't rely on it in whatever way. If you resubmitted this record and to bring me more information about the person who was treated at the hospital at that day, then I will reconsider my results, but I have no basis for changing my decision at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what I'm asking you, though, is why not if you have this alternative put her in your spreadsheet, because you did that with Hasan Kurspahic, and apparently you also did that with Hasan Kustura, so those are two instances where you provided the alternative. Why not do that with Ismeta?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I already promised you to provide you with the revised spreadsheet with all alterative matters, so you will have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I'm asking why you didn't do that in here.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: My answer was given already earlier today when I said I checked and included in the spreadsheet all names that were provided, and for Hasan Kustura, two names were provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And for -- but you're telling us today that for Ismeta Kurspahic, two names were provided.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, I never said that for Ismeta Kurspahic, two names were provided by the Prosecution team. I never said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I see. I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I said in that census data, 1991 census data, there were more than one Ismeta Kurspahic found, and this is in the clarification. And this is, you know, in able 8 that you can check the details in Annex A of these persons, so it is all there. It is a matter of just going through the clarification. And all cases, questionable cases of alleged survivors are explained in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the first questionable one that I'd like to talk about, which is back to page 2 of 16, number 30, Aner Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Of what significance is it that the mother's name is listed as Latifa Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What's the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is his mother's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And his sister, his -- he has two sisters listed: Sejla and Lejla?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: May I have one comment only, please, before you go further. There is a typo in the spreadsheet in the age of the person. It says 60. It should be 6. I'm sorry for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I wasn't even going to point that out.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But this is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Because the date of birth at 1982 puts the child's age at approximately 10 years old.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But what was interesting is, though, is in the indictment, he was listed as 6 years old.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: He was listed as 6 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So whoever reported him might have been guessing as to his age, might have been distant enough in relation to not know he's 10 versus 6.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I told you, people are very bad in remembering dates. Think of yourself. Do you remember all the dates of your relatives?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: God, no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: As simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yeah. But there is some ICRC data that he was reported missing, and the date of disappearance was May 29th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why not exclude him from your list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, it is not me who includes or excludes victims from the indictment of Lukic and Lukic; second, the P119 is a simple overview of information on the victims found in related sources of information. So this is a material to work with, right? And not to immediately exclude or include victims from the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you have the ability to check the ICRC and tell who reported the person missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We don't have the information about the informants. I would have to contact the ICRC back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be significant that his mother Latifa had reported him missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who reported. If it was Latifa, it is Latifa. What can I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you can say she's on your list as well.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, she is, but she's indicated as a potential survivor. This information is already since September in the spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you would agree that the boy listed as Aner Kurspahic is the listed son of Latifa Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think the boy, we have checked the entire household of Latifa Kurspahic, her husband, Omer, Lejla, Aner, the other third child, everybody's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you discover that his father Omer was reported missing to the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I guess it is in my clarification. We can check this. I'm rather sure, yes, that we say, yes, that Omer Kurspahic -- on page 18, please, paragraph in which we discuss the case of Latifa and Lejla Kurspahic. We say Omer Kurspahic and Aner Kurspahic are both listed as still missing by ICRC as of 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just to clarify, when did you indicate Latifa as a potential survivor? In the clarification?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, she's indicated as a potential survivor in the P119, in the version which we've been going through today, which is the same as the one submitted in September last year with my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I guess the issue I have with that is, is in your clarification you're -- we now get specific responses to individual people and their potential to be survivors. Why not alert us by a similarly exhaustive report attached to the original P119 that could tell us all, Hey, there's a problem?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, a good point, I guess. It would be very helpful to have this report, but as far as I remember, it was a rushed testimony in September, and we didn't have enough time to clarify things. And the plan was I would explain about how P119 was made, who made it, and what was the purpose of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, if testimony's been presented that Latifa and her family were not part of any incident on June 14th in Pionirska and those several people associated with her were not there for hypothetical purposes, and considering that your compilation of the list was rushed and could not be verified --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, that misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I was waiting for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It was rushed.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No. No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Didn't you say rushed?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Rushed. The testimony was rushed. There was no time during my testimony to explain all the details of my work. The compilation of P119, believe me, wasn't rushed, wasn't rushed at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. So in that compilation, you see that Latifa voted and registered to vote?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is in the spreadsheet, as out-of-country voter, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that something you could have followed up on? Did you have the resources to follow up on that and report your findings to the OTP or the Court?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, sir. I am -- this is not my task to follow up on these kind of cases. My task is to pinpoint, to highlight these kind of cases, and this is where my task ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Can we have the next page, please, 3 of 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And ma'am, can we take Aner Kurspahic off this list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Latifa, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Her son Aner.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Why? Why would we do that? Not that I have in the spreadsheet any evidence of Aner surviving. On the contrary, we agreed he was still missing person by ICRC, by mid-2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But ma'am, buy see, the problem I have is that your report makes a very specific assertion. When you list the place of death in anywhere as being on the date of June 14th and/or at Pionirska, there is the weight of your profession and your credibility behind that.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What was your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we take him off the list of dead for Pionirska, June 14th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, if we go and look again at this record, why would I do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The date of his mother reporting him missing at 5-29-1992 might be a good start.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is the date last seen. It is perfectly possible that the mother had seen him last time at the end of May. There is no contradiction between these two dates, unless you know more than I do, then please let me know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I will stay. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, if we move forward, there is no corresponding ICRC information or missing persons reports for all but one of the persons listed on page 3 of 16, and please tell me if there's anything on the Book of Dead for any of these people.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So you are speaking of cases 43 to 59, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I'm actually speaking of 31 through 41 on page 3 of your report. And before we get there, ma'am, Aner Kurspahic was listed in the Book of Dead at June 14th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who could list him there but his mother, let's say?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, these are questions that I cannot answer because the sources for the BBD records are enormous. On the first place, witness statement; further, any published list of victims; locally published books of missing; ICRC records of missing persons; local records of missing persons, and many, many other sources. And I have no information about who for each record was the particular informant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. So you can't -- you can't assume reliability of the Book of Dead?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well it is -- I never claimed that I've been using the Bosnian Book of Dead as one of my major sources on victims, and also not on this project. I have never said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so of the persons listed on page 3 of 16 and the corresponding references on page 11 of 16, it appears that many more people are listed in the Book of Dead versus actually having been reported to the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's generally the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is there the possibility that that is because the Book of Dead merely absorbed, let's say, the list from the indictment because it's a highly publicised situation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There is such a possibility, but not only that. There will be that ICRC lists were absorbed, possibly the indictment lists, possibly their witness statements, possibly other sources. This is -- the Bosnian Book of Dead is a very large database that accepted in several cases informants that wouldn't be accepted for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I don't mean to back up a little bit, but that Hasena, last name unknown, can we take the person that has no corresponding data, not even a last name or an age, can we take them off the list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I will answer by asking you a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What should we do about the victims of the Cambodian conflict of Khmer Rouge? There are no names. There are no lists, but there are estimates that from approximately 1 to 3 million were killed. Does it mean that this conflict never happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Let me put to you this, ma'am: Your method of compiling records is inappropriate in a first-commission murder case. It may be fine for the Khmer Rouge or Srebrenica, but when you're going accuse a human being of pulling the trigger on one other human being, you better get both IDs right. That's my -- what I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. Dr. Tabeau has never said anything about who pulled the trigger in any of her submissions or in any of her testimony. She is simply not a part of her evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's quite so. It was more in the form of a comment, anyhow. Let's proceed. You should be coming to a close now, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Next page, please, 4 of 16, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, actually, looking at the previous page and the top of page 4, and top of page 4 is the one I would like to focus on, is these are the two references to Hasan Kurspahic. It's the bottom of page 3 and the top of page 4, the two different Hasans.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, like I said, this is the second instance where you actually put the two similar names in the chart. Why making the decision point with the two Hasans, please?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is not me who put these two names on the list. I received the two names of Hasan Kurspahic, one aged 49, one aged 50, from the Prosecution team for my checks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, we don't have Hasan number 41 voting, but we also don't have him on the International Red Cross, but we do have the second Hasan voting for three years.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is what we see in P119.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Of what significance is it that you see the one Hasan voting for three years?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is a very strong indication that this person is possibly a survivor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And not just a survivor but not a victim of Pionirska.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we take him off the list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is not my decision. Why are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And just looking, though, at the corresponding information, though. In the back, pages 11 -- you have, again, only the report in the Book of Dead but not the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What case are you talking about now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The two Hasans.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just the N-side.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Pages 11 and 12 is where they're referenced.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For one of them, for number 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Right. The reason I ask you, you were given two names of Hasan, but yet the number 26 on the indictment, he's only mentioned once. So, again, tell me how you received information that both may be dead, or was there -- was there a quandary there?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I received two names to search for and check and provide my results back to the Prosecution team. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next two names, Hasiba and Hasnija, and in fact the next four names have no corresponding census data associated with them. Regardless of where the information came from, how significant is that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I think that there is no census data for Hasiba. There is no census data for Hasnija, but for next two persons -- sorry, for next person, Hata, there is a very poor census record with a very deficient JMBG; and then for number 47, Igabala Kurspahic, there is a census record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely. I wasn't -- and while -- I apologise for the translation. But with regards to the other four mentioned, there is no corresponding -- excuse me, three mentioned, then. I stand corrected. There was no corresponding census data.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is -- you have to refer to the concrete names, and then we can follow this. No census for Hasiba, which is number 43 in the spreadsheet; no census for Hasnija, 44; but 45, we have had census record; for 46, Ifeta, there is no census record; 47, Igabala, we do have a census record; 48, Ismet, we have a census record; so this is where we stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And I think you stated on direct exam when you first testified here that the 1991 census is your main data set with other ones taking a supporting role.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't remember what I said exactly, but as a matter of fact, it is the core source in our databases, the census, not population census, of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you go to the corresponding references for the Book of Dead, one Hasnija has no -- or she does have a case ID.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: She does have a case ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So these four people, the next four that I said didn't have any biographical or census data appear magically in the Book of Dead.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether magically, but they do appear in the Bosnian Book of Dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How significant is it that they all have the same three dates of birth, January 1st? They all appear to be born on new year's?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Very good. This is the way they call that unknown day and month of -- of date. 01, 01. So I wouldn't take this 01, 01, as the 1st of January. That would be wrong. This is the BBD coding, and I know something a little bit, believe me. So it is basically the year of birth that is known.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you confirm the year of birth without having a census data to correspond to that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, if I don't have the census record, I can only judge the year of birth from the approximate age of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I ask you that is that on several of the entries, the estimated age from the indictment is actually a few years off, sometimes close, but a few years off from the actual JMBG and census data. Can you explain that.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think I already gave this explanation, but I will repeat. It is because people don't remember dates. People know approximately what age the person was, but they don't remember the exact date of birth unless it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You also asked him whether he remembered the dates of birth of his relatives, and he said, God, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Dates of birth, no. Ages, I tend to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But again, would be these ages -- exact ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But my real point is, ma'am, is that the more data that actually corresponds directly or exactly to the reported information gives you a greater comfort.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Oh, definitely. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at the top --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are we at page 4 of -- can we go to page -- the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at the top is Latifa, and below is Lejla. But you also list as the daughter again as Sejla; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just look in Latifa's L and L relatives, and that's where I'm getting this from.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There is a certain Sejla, but I suggest we check the family of Latifa in the clarification, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in the clarification, I understand, but if there has been testimony that Latifa had a 6-month-old daughter at the time, would 6 months versus two years be the kind of thing that you would say is somewhat consistent, and therefore maybe a mistake was made with the name or spelling as you stated?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, two years, six months, who knows, but what's your point? What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, my point is Latifa's alive and her daughter Lejla's alive.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I am very happy for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Me too.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Exactly. What's the next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What significance is it that the next one, Majda, has no corresponding biographical data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Who doesn't have? Majda?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Majda after -- after Lejla.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it. Number 54, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, this only means that this record wasn't found in the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please remember to pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if there's been sworn testimony and the only sworn testimony related to Majda that never heard of this person, would that support your not finding any census data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This has nothing to do with me finding or not finding this name in the census data. My job is -- you know, has nothing to do with witnesses and their testimonies. I have names and work with names and other biographical details and search for them in my sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The reason I'm arguing with you is quite simply because how you titled your document. You title it as a proof of death, and that to me is a very specific goal, if you will, or mantra for this particular document. And so call me strange, but I think you should be either proving or disproving that fact based on your -- the job you've been asked to do. Do you see why I'm having trouble?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But I don't think you should have any trouble here. Because if you would have read the clarification carefully, you would see that this is the Proof of Death Project of the demographic unit. So this is the -- how we call it, this kind of practices internally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's just a title. Just a title.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well -- but then let me put this to you, ma'am. I suggest that it's more important than that because if they're using you to prove or assist in proving death and someone could go to gaol for killing someone that's alive, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not going to allow that. Ask another question, and -- this is going on a bit too long now, Mr. Alarid. Do you have anything more?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a long list. The problem is if we were dealing with five people, we'd be dealing with five people. We're dealing with 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does that mean that you intend to go through --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I've been skipping a lot, if you can't tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where are you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm at victim number -- well, 57 on the list right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And here again, there appears to be no corresponding biographical data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For number 57, you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Obviously no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. And what significance is that to your -- because I guess what I'm asking you is, what statistical or demographical significance is this report if we cannot extrapolate an error rate of any kind from the data sets as compared to each other?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, sir, indeed there is no error estimate. There is no statistics other than the few numbers in the clarification. However, you must agree with me that the results of these searches have increased our knowledge about the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I also think that some questions have been raised, especially when people are found to be living or there's mistakes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: And very good. I like the questions, because this was a challenge for us to double-check these records, and a lot of things have been clarified. Instead of 31 alleged survivors that you claimed in your motion, we ended with far, far less. You agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We'll agree to disagree, because I don't even know the final answer yet, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I'm willing to concede that we're -- we have differences. But do you think it's significant that Mr. Lukic -- the Lukics are accused of killing these people with specificity and that there are errors in that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I am not allowing that. Ask another question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to focus down on number 67 and 68.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The Ramizas. Do you have any information with regards to why you would put -- because I misspoke. You actually put double names on three people: Hasans Kusturas, the Hasans Kurspahic, and now the Ramiza Kurspahic, two different ages. Can you comment on why they would both be there, considering that only, I believe, one is mentioned on the indictment?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would have to check on the indictment, indeed, which I have and can check immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I have a copy for you, if you would like.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Oh, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I see one Ramiza, age 57 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So you might be right about this, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And again, why put two when the age disparity is so huge?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, not that I'm sure I received two names, but I can check this. But as I said, the practice was to work with the names as receive. So this is probably the most likely explanation. Otherwise, if you look at the age and the relatives, you most certainly must agree with me that these are two different persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Just a moment, Your Honour. I'm just reviewing --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to put to you, though, that one of the VG witnesses that has testified here clarified a clarification that Ramiza Kurspahic were not victims and should not be on the list of victims, how would that impact the validity of this document?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would ask which one? In addition to these two here in the indictment list, there are more in the census as you can read on page 19 of my clarification in the context of searches for Ramiza Kurspahic. There were at least four persons with these names registered in the census. So, sir, you must remember that if a witness says Ramiza Kurspahic, we don't yet know which Ramiza Kurspahic this witness meant unless there is additional information provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, if there was only one on the indictment and one of the named relatives says, Take her off, would you defer to that person?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I, again, would work with the statistical data and the sources I have because this is what I do, and I don't work with witnesses. If there was a witness, then I'm sure the Prosecution team will take care of it at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A moment, Your Honour, to confer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would point you out to one more, and it's Kada Kurspahic, listed as victim number 35. Alphabetically, I think that's back a couple pages on the bottom of page 4 of 16.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Thirty-five, the number 35 in the indictment, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In the indictment. She's number 51 in your table.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be significant and confirmed, also, by your table that she had the maiden name of Sehic?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, not that I can see it from this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Will you go to the Sehic alphabetically on 84 of your table. And looking just at the same, corresponding names and relations, can you verify that they're the same person by your own data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I don't have enough information to confirm -- to agree or disagree with you, except for the fact that is a certain Kada reported with two different family names; similar age, 39, 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But what about JMBG numbers?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, there is no JMBG numbers for this Kada.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: On --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For the other one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 84?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For the other one, yes. There is a JMBG.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so by simple cross-referencing, should you be able to see that they're the same person?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There is no simple cross-referencing. I need to know more details about the persons in order to agree or disagree, that these two are the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: From an accuracy perspective, though, when you find out or discover that there's a duplication by virtue of maiden name, married name, shouldn't you make -- or shouldn't that be part of your reliability coefficient?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is not how the people are reported in the census that, you know, you can have maiden names in the census reported together with husbands' names for women. Women will be reported under husbands' names, and they are no more part of the parental household, so there is -- I really need more information about the persons. I need the names. I need the date of birth. I need the place of birth, these kinds of things. Then I can work with this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Might it be more difficult also just for following up today simply because if even have you a survivor, they might be listed under the husband's household, and there's been no other census since 1991?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, there has been no census, we know that. So there is no reference source, as a matter of fact, for the post-conflict population.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And a follow-up, what's the CIPS system?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Now, you tell me because what's in your list, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if you've been made aware of it.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I have made aware myself of this system until you raised your list of survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. What's your understanding of this list, and could it have assisted you with your research?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, on survivors, probably yes. However, not the way you did it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I have no doubt.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Okay. Great. We agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But we did find them.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll pass the witness at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, I imagine to continue the pattern initiated by Mr. Alarid, you will now be either examining or re-examining, not cross-examining. Proceed anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, thank you very much for returning to testify again in this case. Based on your lengthy experience working on matters relating to proof of death in many cases at the ICTY and according to your particular expertise, victims lists in indictment schedules are often based upon information from those who survived as to those who died. Would you say that's correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: On survivors' recollections, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So would you say it is true that the purpose of the Proof of Death Project, as you've titled it, is to corroborate the information contained in the indictment schedules along with evidence of witnesses, family members, victims, through the use of several sources available to the demographics unit?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you do this by using your expert skills in analysis of data sources; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, would it be correct to say that the more detail provided by survivors as to those who died, the better equipped the demographics unit is to corroborate those victims in the data sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And so it flows from that that the more details provided by the survivors as to those who died and the better equipped your unit is to corroborate the deaths or disappearances of those persons, the more reliable the results; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you agree that in some cases due to a lack of extensive information as to the precise date of birth, father's name of the victim, you were not able to corroborate the deaths or disappearance of a few of the names with complete certainty?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Whereas in other cases you were, in fact, able to match, to corroborate the deaths or disappearance of named victims with a higher degree of certainty?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So now logically, if a large number of persons were killed and if there was no one who could provide information as to their names, dates of birth, father's names, and information about other relatives, it would be exceedingly difficult if not impossible for your unit to obtain reliable matches which could corroborate the deaths or disappearance of those persons. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, if there are no survivors and no record from surviving family members, friends, neighbors, then it's hardly possible to find the victims, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So this means, therefore, that in war crimes cases where forensic evidence of death may not be available due to lack of access or destruction or deterioration of the physical evidence or lack of resources, the only way the deaths can be proven is through witness evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for a legal conclusion, compound question, and argumentive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This witness is an expert in exactly this area of providing corroboration as to proof of death in war crimes cases. I think she is eminently qualified to comment on whether this is the common practice in war crimes cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to allow it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So I will go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In war crimes cases where evidence of forensic evidence of death may not be available due to some of the factors I listed as well as others, the only way that deaths can be proven is through a combination of witness evidence corroborated through, for example, the very project which your unit undertook in the Lukic case and in the Srebrenica case. Would you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Most definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you agree that the bottom line in all of this is even in the case of statistically reliable matches, until and unless there is actual physical evidence as in actual remains exhumed and an autopsy performed with a DNA analysis, until that time an analysis such as the Proof of Death Project can merely serve to corroborate the witness evidence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's very correct. Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That said, however, you would agree that there is a possibility of reaching a high -- of reaching a certain number of highly reliable matches in a variety of sources; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can I ask for P119 to be placed on the ELMO. This is just a colour version. It's purely as a demonstrative exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, in the Lukic and Lukic case, the Prosecution engaged the demographics unit in a Proof of Death Project during the summer of 2008; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And it took three demographers in your demographics unit approximately three weeks to complete this analysis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it would be three weeks for the first initial wave of searches. It took much longer than three weeks to go through the records, results and analyse and summarise this. And it took, again, recently a lot of time three demographers, two additional rounds of searches.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As we look at the coloured chart in front of us, which is a coloured version of P119, you see the original results of the Proof of Death Project; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, in the case of -- sorry. In the case of alleged --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we have a hard copy of this material because it is not the same as P119, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It's the same as P119, Your Honour, but I have copies to hand out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, the bottom is not the same. Actually, the top is. Thank you. And just for the record, just in the interest to speed up all those things, I think that most of questions and answer is just heard that we have in reports, which we have from this witness, actually, expert. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, in the case of alleged victims whose records could not be matched in one or more sources, those cases could still serve as corroboration of the death or disappearance of that victim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, outside the scope of this person's expertise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, can I have the transcript back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I have to rule on the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This goes to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, the question is about the empty cells, what is the meaning of empty cells and no matches reported in P119. No match obtained. Does it mean that a person is fictitious? Doesn't mean anything. It only means that we did not find a record of this person in a given source. There might be other evidence including witness statements, witness testimonies, whatever other sources that might be corroborating the fact that the person died at certain moment in certain circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. So then with the exception of the one typo that you cited, which was that a zero was added onto the 6 next to Aner Kurspahic, which is purely a typo, as said, there can be no errors, but rather, there can indeed be inconsistencies in the matching. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, inconsistencies can be -- yes, I agree, no errors, but inconsistencies. But I wouldn't think of on the first place of inconsistencies in matching, although there might be some. There will be inconsistencies between the sources, how things are reported in the sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Right so in other words, inconsistencies, which may be seen in P119 represent accurately reported data from two sources which were inconsistent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. There might be differences in how the date of birth is reported in two sources, how the date of disappearance is reported. That is perfectly possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the results of the Proof of Death Project, which are represented in this Exhibit P119, began with a starting point which is reflected in yellow. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. This is information that was sent to us, and actually most of it comes from the indictment schedules. Some records are additional as we heard today, but they are all included as were sent to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And then following that initial starting point, there were essentially three steps to the Proof of Death Project conducted by the demographics unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the first step which is reflected in green on this demonstrative exhibit was to search for data that this person may have been present in Visegrad before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. That is the reference source, the 1991 population census, reporting on the population of Visegrad in the outbreak of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Right. Now, the second step reflected in blue was to search for data tending to show that this person may have survived the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. The blue colour relates to three voters registers from 1997, 1998 in 200 elections, and one more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just for the record, those blue columns, we hadn't in a previous document P119. So there is changes between this document and the previous one, just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the way that the previous document was loaded into e-court, it had to be cut because of the width of the document. So the P119 which is eight pages was rendered in e-court as a document with 16 pages, so in that respect it's correct. And also, this has been colour-coded for the purpose of this methodology discussion. That's the only change that has been made to P119. Otherwise it is exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The contents are the same?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The contents are 100 per cent the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And if I may add, I have been using this with Mr. Alarid, and we had exactly identical information in his version of P119 and in this colour of coded version I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is not 100 per cent the same content because we have new columns now. Survivor -- step 2, date of survival of this person after the war. In this column, we could find for some of person that they survived after the war, such as Hasan Kurspahic and some others, so I didn't have time to check everything. That is the change, and that is the clear evidence that this table is not the same as the previous one, especially not 100 per cent. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Cepic didn't look closely at P119 before. And now that its highlighted in blue, it's more evidence, but it's exactly the same columns. What has been added is the three steps to explain the methodology, which comes right from Dr. Tabeau's clarification. This is just a simplified method of explaining the underlying methodology. The contents in the column, the labeling in the column, everything in the chart was taken exactly from P119, and it -- certainly if Mr. Cepic finds anything that's different in any entries, please call that to our attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, still not satisfied?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. For example, number 52, we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you what, Mr. Cepic. We're going to take the break now, and you can discuss it over tea with Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alarid, I am to ask you, are you still calling Dr. Andersen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are preparing his 94 quater motion because of the Department of Defence's failure to give permission to Dr. Anderson. He's also a reserve colonel in the army, and they denied permission of him, and under suspicious circumstances because they approached him as to who are you going to testify for, and he couldn't remember because he had only dealt with the burn victim, and the Department of Defence handed him a hundred pages on Milan Lukic. So it seems to me that there was some prompting behind him being denied because he didn't -- the impetus wasn't him. So I'm not sure what our remedy is at this point, but we would -- I mean I think his report is valuable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He may not be with us, but if you're going to file a motion, then file it, and we'll deal with it. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask Mr. Alarid to confirm on the record that tomorrow morning we will have Jenkins and that he will be followed by Hough.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, Hough and then Jenkins, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, in the afternoon. So we are now switching the order an additional time, and we are calling Hough. We still have not received the final packet of what appears to be several thousands of pages of source material.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's just everything that he brought with him. That's what I brought. That's what the Court ordered, and I didn't want to short-change you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may be having an application after I seen the total bulk of material we're receiving tonight. It seems impossible to read in preparation for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I heard that argument about four or five years ago in another case. We're going to take the break now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, just before we took a break, you had told us of the three steps, or you had -- I think you had concluded the second step, so you explained the starting point, you explained step 1, which is collecting data on the presence of the victim in Visegrad before the war; step 2, data on survival of this person or evidence of survival of this person after the war. Now, the third step which is represented in violet on this demonstrative exhibit was to search for data which tended to show that the person was recorded in databases of the dead or the missing. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the methodology behind the Proof of Death Project, both the initial phase that was done to prepare P119, as well as the follow-up clarification in response to the Defence motion, all of that is in evidence, and the Chamber can consider any of that in more detail if they choose to. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask for a clarification. Is it in evidence? I don't believe it is in evidence. I believe it's part of a motion and it's attached to the motion, but that's the difference between -- because I have not stipulated to the admission of her clarification report from an evidentiary perspective, and we would have a motion on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As far as I know, Your Honours, it was admitted as Exhibit P300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It had been admitted as Exhibit P300, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then it would be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Tabeau, the sources which your unit used in conducting these searches in seeking to corroborate the witness evidence are represented by the top row of the spreadsheet in green, blue, and the violet portions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now by comparison with these numerous data sources used by your unit in conducting its analysis, it's not fully clear from the Defence motion precisely what the sources were which were used to result in their submission. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it is, because the two lists the Defence retained from the RS authorities included no explanation as to what sources were used for the compilation of this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the sources which have been mentioned by the Defence include the Visegrad MUP and the RS government and a personal investigation conducted by the Defence team and the telephone book. Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yeah, it's about right. I think it's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the sources used by the Visegrad MUP and the RS government are similarly not known; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. There is nothing about what are the underlying sources used for compiling these two lists, not in the correspondence that was attached to the Defence motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And the requests sent by the Defence to the Visegrad MUP and the RS government did not contain any information about the relatives of those named; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. What was sent was just the indictment list for Pionirska and Bikavac, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge, neither the RS government nor the Visegrad MUP have access to the 1991 census; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, assumes facts not in evidence and calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This is directly in the area of Dr. Tabeau's expertise. It's also contained in the clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's really an objection without merit. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave, the speakers, have been speaking quite fast, so the interpreters could not catch the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask both of you to ensure that there's a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, as the telephone book lists nothing --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But I didn't give the answer yet about the census, so the question was whether the RS authorities do have access to the census data. They don't. They don't have the individual census records. Not even the statistical authority of Republika Srpska in Banja Luka has the individual census records.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, as the telephone book lists nothing more than first name and last name, the telephone book records have little to no value in an analysis such as this. Would you say that's accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We made it in a table in the clarification which shows the frequencies of certain surnames in the census. So if you look for certain names, even if it is first name and surname, a combination of the two, there is no reason to believe that by using this first name and surname or just the surname as the Defence did, you would be able to ever narrow down your search. It is simply impossible because many people have the same names, and still there will be different persons. There is a surname included in our clarification which has a frequency in the census of several thousand. If I may refer to this table, this is table 15, and the name Jasarevic, table 15, page 31 in the clarification, the surname Jasarevic in Bosnia has 6.436 individuals at least, with the surname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: With that surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And this is not taking into account the possible misspellings, which would still represent the same name. So what I'm saying, there are even more than what I have in table 15. So searching in telephone books for a person using a surname or even a first name in combination with a surname has no point because this is too little information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But it might be a little more accurate or helpful if you had the first name and the surname.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is really helpful is next to the first name, surname, father's name is needed, date of birth is needed, because this is how we uniquely identify individuals. People are different, even though they may carry the same names. But where they were born, where they live, household composition and stuff, this is what makes people different, and that is not what can be seen from telephone books. It is just a coincidence that the surname of a given time is mentioned there or a combination of first name and surname is there. This doesn't mean anything yet. So the whole thing is about when searching for survivors to identify potential candidates and then to narrow down the search results. And it certainly cannot be done using the telephone book records. There is no point in doing this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, Exhibit P300, which is your clarification, is a direct and detailed response to the Defence allegations contained in their motion per victim. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And in that clarification, in Exhibit P300, there is a table called table 3 which essentially summarises your conclusions or the results of your additional searches that you conducted for P119 but now in response to the Defence allegations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can I ask the court usher to hand out a demonstrative blow-up of table 3 from that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just a copy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I hope my assumption that this witness's testimony will be concluded today is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: From my perspective, absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you going have any re-examination, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm up to four questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Tabeau, as we look at this table we see the names which were contested in the Defence motion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the yellow starting point is the direct excerpt from P119 in relation to those victims named in the Defence motion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And thereafter, we see the date of birth as reported in the 1991 census, also directly extracted from P119; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the next columns reflected in rust colour reflect the Defence claims as outlined in your clarification; and the final column, peach colour, reflects the results of your analysis per victim mentioned in the Defence claims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, all these results per victim are included in P300 just to be complete; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There are specific descriptions for every victim one by one in the clarification, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The results of P119 are in fact bolstered and confirmed by your clarification, which is now admitted as Exhibit P300. Would you say that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: May I have a copy as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It's table 3 from the clarification. Did I -- I handed out six copies. I have a few more. They're a bit folded, but I have a few more.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Tabeau, the transcript did not record your answer to the last question. I asked you simply whether the results of P119 are bolstered and confirmed by Exhibit P300. Would you say that's correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, before I finish, I'd like to go back to your discussion earlier of your policy of being conservative in your analysis. So does this mean, if I understand it correctly, that if you did not have enough data to accurately distinguish between two potential matches, one a potential victim and one a potential survivor, you erred on the side of including the potential survivor in your results. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is the correct answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So it is possible that someone listed on P119 as a potential survivor might in fact be dead.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, contrary to assertions, therefore, that the victim list has been inflated, the methodology of your process, of your analysis, if anything, would result in an underestimation of the number of victims. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That was the purpose of this exercise, to highlight the potential survivors.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, unless you have any further matters for me to cover, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the only proof of death projects you've done were for this case and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For several other cases, and this is an ongoing work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This is an ongoing matter?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Are other cases ongoing matters?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... deal with?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I actually missed your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: With this one having 80-some names, what were the numbers you were dealing with in the other seven cases?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say seven cases. I said several cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Several cases.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Several, of which several still are ongoing, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What's several, if you can give us an exact number?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right now two more cases at least and probably two more coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many people are you dealing with in those cases?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this does not relate to anything covered in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask another question. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And for reference, Your Honour, she made a comparison between Srebrenica and this case, for reference, and I was asking for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I rule it doesn't arise. Please ask another question, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Have you ever done this for a first-commission accused?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would say, sir, I do it whenever requested, and I don't really distinguish between cases. It is just a standard approach, so it really doesn't matter what kind of case I'm working on. It is still for me the same type of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. That's not the question I asked you, though, ma'am. Have you ever done it for a first-commission accused versus something that's more non-specific?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is not something that Dr. Tabeau would have any reason to know. It's not part of her expertise, and it's not a matter that she can be expected to comment upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And it doesn't arise. Did you examine the witness in this -- on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, certainly not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that every Yugoslav citizen was required to have a JMBG number?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And those JMBG numbers is a data set that can be accessed by the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are all questions which could have been covered in chief. These just don't arise from cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They came out of cross. I mean, come on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And of the JMBG numbers, every person should have one regardless of changing their name from married to maiden or vice versa?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The number JMBG was introduced around 1980, and since then every child born from that moment on and later was receiving a JMBG issued at birth. All other persons were requested to arrange receiving this number through other channels, but as a matter of fact since 1980 every citizen of the former Yugoslavia has a JMBG.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, let's just go to your table 3 from the clarification, and let's start at the bottom. Sada Turjacanin. She is a scheduled victim in the indictment; true?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, she is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And she is named with that name originally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Am I leading?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. Apart from leading, I presented table 3, but we did not go through the details of each victim, and this was something that the Defence extensively covered in chief, victim per victim discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not allowing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, you mean to tell me you're not going to -- you don't want to hear about Sada Turjacanin's sister?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing it. Please, ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you not want to hear about Sada Turjacanin's sister?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have ruled. Ask another question. If you have no more questions, we'll conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You talked about corroborating data; correct? And you referred to your clarification; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do to corroborate the assertions of the Prosecution regarding to the -- that the Sada Turjacanin as alleged in the Defence motion is a different person?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There is a paragraph in my clarification. We can refer to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's not the question I asked. I go, What did you do?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I did search for this person in the census, and there is a table in Annex A of my clarification in which this record is reviewed. This person is also known as Sadeta Turjacanin, and there is a date of birth of this person which is 9th July, 1963, which is fully consistent with the age of 29 in the indictment for this victim. Moreover, I checked the census record and compared how this person was reported in any other source, and there is no information about that this person would register as a voter, and there is no information that the person is reported as a dead person. But this simply means that I have no demographic evidence that I can use to corroborate or reject what is in the indictment based on the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you confirm a JMBG number to correspond with the date of birth as given?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, sir, we can refer to that census record of this person, which is in table 16. And as we know, I hope you know, date of birth is part of the JMBG. In table 16 on page 31, we have the JMBG of this victim of this person, which says we are speaking of Sadeta Turjacanin, father's name Surijo [phoen], born on 9th of July, 1963. Then you look at the JMBG. It's available. Seven first digits represent the date of birth. It is all consistent. Further, the region is consistent. It is Visegrad. Further, there is a number for sex coding. It's consistent. So what's your problem with this? I did check what I supposed to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How about the difference in father's name?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In father's name?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: How do you know that her father has a different name? I can't see it from the relatives column in the P119. Perhaps you have additional information that you didn't share with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What about what information that you have?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: My information is as in table 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so that's all you did to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, I did -- this is not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. What else did you do?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I did check all other sources, and I told you, she didn't register to vote. She didn't register as an internally displaced person or a refugee.
