She wasn't reported as dead or missing person. At the same time, I know that there is a certain person, Zehra Turjacanin, who gave a statement this person, and she's mentioning two of them. One being totally unrelated to a victim, and another one being the victim. So it all comes together. This is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So based solely on the testimony and by hearsay, you get this information. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, that's not what I'm saying. Based on my searches of identifying this person in the census, on information about how the person possibly was reported or not reported in other sources on survivors, on deaths, on missing persons, and in addition to this, based on the results of the investigation of the Prosecution team, my conclusion is that there is no reason to mark this person as a potential survivor or unrelated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What specifically did you do for the other Bikavac victims as alleged in your table?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just renew my previous objection that this is a victim-by-victim questioning which could have been done in chief and does not arise in cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing it. I'm losing my patience. Bring this re-examination to a close. You have asked more than enough questions, and we're not getting anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would pass the witness, and I would move to strike the witness's clarification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- based on the fact of her admission that there is no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You move to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To strike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To remove it from evidence as being unreliable, as being statistically not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't make that submission now. Make that in your -- make that at some other time. That's not how we operate here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't make a submission like that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You admitted it orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is not the time to make submissions of that kind. You can file a motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They moved it into evidence, orally, Your Honour, without a witness present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are going to adjourn until tomorrow afternoon. If you wish to file a motion, then you can file it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one matter. It's seven hours after I was told I would have the source material. Throughout the afternoon, we are getting copies of witness statements that we -- ICTY statements that given the Defence. All we want, I think the spirit of the Court's order, all we need to prepare our examination are Dr. Hough's notes, source material of his interview, and tests of Milan Lukic. It seems that we're playing some game here where we run the clock until quarter to 7.00 and then we don't get it, and then tomorrow morning perhaps we get it. It's a simple matter -- now with a smirk on the face, we now get announced that we have it in the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, when are these personal attacks going to end from Mr. Groome. When are they going to end, Your Honour? We have limited resources in the Defence. We have one copy that's been working ever since we came in here non-stop with our legal assistant, sitting there copying every document in the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How far have you gotten in providing the material?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have another two packets here, Your Honour. I don't know, I've been sitting here listening to the witness, as you have, Your Honour. I've just been acting as a courier to give this documentation to the Prosecution and complying with their request that I note when there are hand-written notes, I have noted that on every single packet that has hand-written notes from Dr. Hough, and I have presented it to them. That's what I've been trying to do to facilitate the matter in the good spirit that the Court told us to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, ensure that all the material is provided as required by the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Am I receiving the notes of Mr. Milan Lukic's interview and the psychiatric test that were performed this evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You are receiving a packet of documents for which there are hand-written notes from Dr. Hough. I have not looked at every page to see what they are. I can't even read some of his writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that all the material that we will be receiving?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, it is not. I just identified that there is more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't want counsel to be speaking across the courtroom to each other. That's not proper. We are going to adjourn. That concludes your evidence, Doctor. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave. In any event, we are adjourning until tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
